When the underside of the pancake is cooked (about 90 seconds), flip it over to cook the other side. Carry on to make 8 thin pancakes – either serving as soon as you cook them or keeping them warm in a low-heat oven until all 8 are ready.

Serve 2 pancakes per person, topped with half a teaspoon of sugar and a lemon quarter for squeezing. (Tip: Orange juice makes a good alternative topping for variety, and children might prefer it to the sour-tasting lemon.)

name: Breakfast fruit salad
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 200g red or green (or both!) seedless grapes, halved
half a melon (cantaloupe or galia), deseeded and chopped

steps: Mix together the sliced kiwi fruit, grapes and melon in a large bowl. (Tip: Remember, if you choose canned fruit, make sure that it's in natural fruit juice, not syrup.)
In a separate bow, mix together the low-fat yoghurt and ginger (if using).

Share the fruit between 4 serving bowls and spoon the yoghurt mixture on top. Information: You can use pretty much any fruit you like for this recipe. Here are some tasty combinations to try:oranges, raspberries and blueberries

name: Apple, apricot and sultana squares
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 1 apple, cored and chopped into small chunks
half a teapsoon ground mixed spice (optional)

steps: Preheat the oven to 180C (fan 160C, gas mark 4). Grease a 23cm (9-inch) shallow square cake tin with a little reduced-fat spread, then line the base with baking parchment or greaseproof paper.
Melt the remaining spread in a large saucepan with the golden syrup. Take care that the mixture doesn't get too hot.

Remove the pan from the heat and add the porridge oats, apple, apricots, sultanas (or raisins) and mixed spice (if using). Stir well. (Tip: If you have a microwave, you can melt the spread and golden syrup in a large microwave-safe bowl for 40 to 50 seconds on high, then add the remaining ingredients as above.)
Add the beaten egg and mix well again.
Tip the mixture into the prepared tin and level the surface. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until firm.
Cool in the tin for about 20 minutes, then cut into 16 squares. (Tip: Store in an airtight container for up to a week, or freeze for up to 3 months.)

name: Tasty chicken wraps
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 130g skinless, boneless roast chicken breasts, chopped
quarter of a cucumber, chopped into small pieces

steps: Lay out the wraps or tortillas on a clean work surface.
Put the soft cheese and yoghurt in a bowl, and mix together until smooth.
Add the chicken, sweetcorn and cucumber. Season with some pepper, then mix well. (Tip: If you're not keen on cucumber or sweetcorn, use grated carrot or some of your favourite veg instead.)
Spread an equal amount of the yoghurt and chicken mixture over each wrap, then top with the lettuce.
Roll up each wrap tightly and slice in half. (Tip: If serving later or adding to a lunchbox, wrap in cling film or foil and keep cool until ready to eat – a small ice pack will help keep them fresh.)

name: Chicken pasta with peas
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 175g cooked chicken, chopped into small chunks

steps: Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Add a pinch of salt and the pasta. Stir once and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, or according to the instructions on the packet, until the pasta is cooked but still slightly firm in the middle.
About 2 or 3 minutes before the pasta is done, add the peas to the water to cook.

Drain the pasta and peas in a colander, then return to the pan. Add the chicken, horseradish, crème fraîche and parsley. Stir well to combine, and season with the pepper. (Tip: Add extra vegetables if you like, such as chopped red pepper and sweetcorn.)
Put the pan back over a low heat and mix gently until everything is just warmed through. Divide evenly between 4 bowls and tuck in!

name: Turkey tikka kebabs
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 500g skinless turkey breast, cut into chunks
1 pepper (any colour), deseeded and cut into chunks
1 green chilli, deseeded and finely chopped

steps: Put the turkey chunks into a bowl (not a metal one) and add the yoghurt, curry paste and coriander (if using). Mix together thoroughly, then cover and chill for at least 20 minutes, though you can leave overnight if you prefer. (Tip: Use chicken instead of turkey, for a change.)

When ready to cook, soak 8 wooden kebab sticks in hot water for a few minutes (this will help prevent them from burning). Put rice on to cook in a large saucepan of gently boiling water. It will take about 30 minutes. (Tip: Wholegrain rice will provide you with more fibre and B vitamins – remember that it takes longer to cook than white rice.)
Thread the turkey chunks, pepper and courgette onto the kebab sticks, alternating the pieces.

Preheat the grill, grill pan or barbecue. Cook the kebabs for 10 to 12 minutes, turning often, until cooked through. (Tip: Make sure the turkey is thoroughly cooked by inserting a sharp knife – there should not be any pink juices.)
Meanwhile, mix together the tomatoes, red onion, chilli and coriander for the relish. (Tip: If you're not keen on coriander or chilli, simply leave them out.)
Serve the relish with the kebabs, along with some lettuce and cucumber.

name: Mushrooms on toast
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 4 handfuls of cup or button mushrooms, washed and sliced

steps: Put the mushrooms and milk into a saucepan, and heat until just boiling. Reduce the heat and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile toast the bread. Spread each slice with lower-fat spread.

Mix the cornflour with 2 tablespoons of cold water, then stir the mixture into the mushrooms. Heat until it thickens (this takes only a few seconds) and cook gently for 1 minute. (Tip: Another time, use the mushroom mixture as a delicious filling for omelettes.)

Divide the mushrooms evenly between the slices of toast and serve straight away. (Tip: You can use regular or mini pitta breads instead of toast if you prefer. Warm the pittas first and stuff them with some shredded lettuce before spooning in the mushrooms.)

name: Hot cheese and salsa turnovers
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 1 small red onion, peeled and finely chopped
quarter of a cucumber, finely chopped
1g finely chopped fresh coriander or parsley, or 1 teaspoon dried mixed herbs (optional)

steps: In a bowl, make the salsa by mixing together the tomatoes, red onion, cucumber and coriander or parsley (if using). (Tip: Fire up the filling a little by adding half a teaspoon of finely chopped red or green chilli – or enough to suit your taste!)
Heat a non-stick frying pan and add a few drops of vegetable oil. Add 1 of the tortillas and turn it in the pan so that its base is lightly oiled.
Sprinkle over a quarter of the salsa mixture, spreading it evenly across the surface. Then sprinkle a quarter of the cheese, and season with black pepper.
Cook over a medium heat for a couple of minutes, until the cheese starts to melt and the tortilla is lightly browned. Fold in half, set aside and keep warm.
Cook the remaining tortillas in the same way. Slice each in half and serve. (Tip: Next time, try using 4 or 5 chopped spring onions instead of red onion.)

name: Slow-cooked lamb and leek bake
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 350g lamb neck fillet, trimmed and chopped into bite-sized chunks

steps: Sprinkle the dried mixed herbs, pepper and flour onto a plate and mix. Roll the cubes of pork in this mixture.
Preheat the oven to 180C (fan 160C, gas mark 4).
Heat a large flameproof casserole dish on the hob and add the vegetable oil. Add the lamb chunks, letting them sear and brown. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until browned on all sides.

Add the onion, leek, carrots, lentils, peas, stock, tomato purée, cumin and paprika. Season with some pepper and stir well to mix. Bring up to the boil, then remove from the heat. (Tip: The cumin and paprika add extra flavour and spiciness, though you could leave them out (or switch them for something else) if you prefer.)
Arrange the sliced potatoes in an overlapping layer to cover the surface of the lamb mixture.

Cover and bake for 75 minutes hours, removing the lid for the final 30 minutes to brown the potatoes. Remove from the oven and leave to stand for 5 minutes before serving. (Tip: Serve with a portion of your favourite green veg – like broccoli, green beans or spinach – to help towards your 5 A Day.)

name: Prawn jambalaya
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 2 handfuls of cup or button mushrooms, sliced

steps: Put the rice into a large saucepan and cook in simmering water for 12 to 15 minutes, or according to instructions on the packet, until tender. Drain well.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan and cook the onion and celery for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened.
Add the green pepper, mushrooms, tomatoes and prawns, and stir-fry for another 4 minutes. (Tip: Next time, try 150g chopped cooked chicken instead of prawns, if you like.)

Stir in the hot cooked rice, parsley, cajun seasoning or paprika and chilli powder. Cook for 2 more minutes, stirring all the time until everything is heated through. (Tip: Save time by cooking the rice in advance, rinsing it with cold water to cool it quickly, then storing in the fridge until needed. Make sure it's reheated thoroughly by adding to the frying pan with the green pepper and mushrooms, and cooking for 3 to 4 minutes before stirring in the tomatoes and prawns.)
Check the seasoning, adding some pepper and an extra pinch of chilli powder if needed. Serve at once.

name: Blueberry and banana muffins
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 125g lower-fat spread, melted and cooled slightly
50g soft brown or light muscovado sugar

steps: Preheat the oven to 180C (fan 160C, gas mark 4). Line a muffin tin with 8 paper muffin cases or squares of baking paper.

Mix together the cooled low-fat spread, milk, vanilla extract, mashed banana, apple purée and eggs in a bowl. (Tip: To make your own apple purée, simmer a chopped cooking apple in a little water for 5 to 6 minutes until tender. Then simply drain, mash and leave to cool.)
In a separate large mixing bowl, combine the flour, mixed spice, sugar, blueberries and porridge oats.
Slowly tip the wet ingredients into the bowl of dry ones, gently mixing as you go, until combined. (Tip: The secret of successful muffins is to avoid over-mixing the wet and dry ingredients.)

Divide the mixture evenly between the muffin cases, then bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until firm and golden. Remove from the oven and leave to cool on a wire rack. (Tip: Next time, try dried cranberries instead of blueberries.)

name: Healthier full English breakfast
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 4 lean back bacon rashers, fat trimmed
250g closed-cup mushrooms, washed and thickly sliced
420g reduced-salt and sugar baked beans in tomato sauce

steps: Preheat the grill. Arrange the bacon and halved tomatoes on the rack and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, turning the bacon once.

Meanwhile, put the mushrooms into a large frying pan with the water. Heat and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. (Tip: Cooking mushrooms in a little water is a much healthier cooking method than frying them.)
At the same time, heat the baked beans in a separate saucepan. (Tip: Make it a habit to choose canned beans with a reduced sugar and salt content.)

Heat the vegetable oil in a non-stick frying pan and crack in the eggs. Cook over a medium heat for about 2 minutes until set, then transfer to the grill to set the surface. At this point, remove the grill pan, and share the bacon and tomatoes between 4 warm serving plates.
Share out the baked beans and mushrooms, then place 1 egg on each plate. Season with black pepper and serve.

name: Kicking prawn salad
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 2 green chillies, deseeded and finely chopped
2 tablespoons fresh coriander (or parsley), finely chopped

steps: Make the dressing by mixing together the oil, lime, chillies and coriander or parsley in a salad bowl. (Tip: If you're not a fan of spice, simply leave the chilli out. Or if you like things particularly spicy, use red chillies instead!)
Add the prawns and stir well to coat. If making ahead, cover and refrigerate until ready to serve (no more than few hours in advance).

When ready to serve, remove the prawns from the fridge. Add the potatoes and tomatoes, season with black pepper and mix well. (Tip: This works best with chopped large tomatoes, but cherry or mini plum tomatoes go well too.)
Arrange the lettuce leaves on 4 serving plates. Spoon the prawn mixture onto each plate

name: Quick chicken couscous
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 250g skinless, boneless roast chicken breasts, chopped

steps: Put the couscous into a large mixing bowl and cover with the hot stock. Leave for 10 to 15 minutes to swell and cool, then stir with to fluff up the grains.

Add the chicken, sweetcorn, tomatoes, cucumber, lemon juice and black pepper. Stir well to mix and then divide between 4 bowls. (Tip: You can make a fruity version of this meal by replacing the sweetcorn, tomatoes and cucumber with chopped apple, seedless grapes, and raisins or chopped ready-to-eat dried apricots.)

name: Tuna, carrot and cheddar patties
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoons fresh parsley or coriander, chopped

steps: Preheat the oven to 200C (fan 180C, gas mark 6). Grease a large baking sheet with a little vegetable oil.

Put the tuna into a large mixing bowl and mash it with a fork. Add the carrots, onion, breadcrumbs, egg, cheese and fresh herbs. Season with some pepper. (Tip: For a vegetarian version, you can replace the tuna with a 150g of marinated tofu pieces, chopped finely.)
Shape the mixture into 6 burger patties and arrange them on the prepared baking sheet.

Bake for about 20 to 25 minutes, until golden brown. Leave to cool for a few minutes, then serve on the lettuce leaves. (Tip: If you're really hungry, serve the patties in warm pitta breads or lightly toasted burger buns.)

name: Pizza crumpets
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Preheat the grill. Toast the undersides of the crumpets until crispy – about 2 minutes. (Tip: Try using wholemeal pitta breads as a change from crumpets. Just skip grilling the underside.)
Remove from the grill, flip the crumpets over and spread each with 1 teaspoon of tomato purée. Arrange the sliced tomatoes on top and grill for 2 minutes.

Sprinkle the herbs and cheese evenly over the crumpets, season with pepper to taste, and grill until the cheese melts and bubbles – another minute or so. Serve at once. (Tip: Add a little chopped cooked ham, chopped cooked chicken or extra vegetables, such as sliced peppers, courgette or mushrooms on the crumpets before sprinkling with the cheese.)

name: Toasted oats with yoghurt and fruit
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Preheat the grill. Spread the porridge oats, nuts and seeds onto a baking sheet and toast them for 1 to 2 minutes. Take care not to burn them! (Tip: If you don't eat nuts, simply leave them out!)
Tip the mixture into a bowl and stir in the yoghurt, apple juice, raisins or sultanas, and grated apples. (Tip: Swap the yoghurt with a soya alternative to make this dairy-free.)
Share between 4 bowls and serve, topped with the grapes. (Tip: You could use blueberries or raspberries (thawed if frozen) instead of grapes.)

name: Caribbean chicken salad
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 150g pineapple pieces in natural juice, drained

steps: Cook the rice in a saucepan of gently boiling water for about 15 minutes, until tender. Drain and rinse under cold water to cool quickly, then drain again.
Mix together the rice, pineapple, bananas, grapes, sultanas or raisins and lemon juice.
In a large bowl, mix together the yoghurt and mayonnaise. Add the rice mixture and chicken. Season with pepper and mix well.
Arrange the lettuce on 4 serving plates and share the chicken mixture between them. Serve at once.

name: Pesto tagliatelle, peppers and squash
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 350g butternut squash, peeled and cut into chunks
1 red pepper, deseeded and cut into chunks
1 yellow pepper, deseeded and cut into chunks
1 medium red onion, peeled and sliced
250g dried tagliatelle (or any long pasta, like spaghetti or linguine)

steps: Preheat the oven to 200C (fan 180C, gas mark 6). Put the butternut squash, peppers and onion into a large roasting tin. (Tip: You can buy pre-prepared butternut squash, or peel and deseed a whole medium-sized one.)
Add the olive oil to the pan and toss to coat the veg. Roast for 30 to 35 minutes, turning once, until tender.
Around 10 minutes before the vegetables are ready, cook the tagliatelle in a large saucepan of boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes.
While the pasta is cooking, use a potato peeler to slice the courgette into long, thin strips. Add these to the tagliatelle to cook for about 3 minutes.
Drain the pasta and courgette, and return to the saucepan. Stir in the pesto sauce and roasted vegetables, along with any juices from the pan.
Season with black pepper and serve, sprinkling 1 teaspoon of grated cheese over each portion.

name: Pork with apples and celery
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 750g potatoes, scrubbed and cut into chunks
1 red apple, cored and cut into 1cm-thick slices
400g pork fillet (tenderloin), sliced into chunks and fat trimmed

steps: Cook the potatoes in simmering water, until tender. They will take about 20 minutes. Drain and put aside when cooked.

Meanwhile, heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a large non-stick frying pan. Add the apple slices, cooking them over a medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side. Add the sugar and cook for another 1 or 2 minutes, until browned. Remove from the pan and set aside. Wipe the pan with kitchen paper.

Roll the pieces of pork fillet in the dried mixed herbs. Heat the remaining oil in the frying pan. Add the pork and cook over medium-heat for a few minutes to brown. (Tip: Another time, try this recipe with turkey breast steaks instead of pork.)
Add the onion and celery, then pour in the stock and apple juice. Leave to simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. The liquid should reduce down a little. Season with pepper.
Mash the potatoes and beat in the milk.

Serve the potatoes with the pork and apples, along with a portion of lightly cooked fresh or frozen vegetables, like broccoli. (Tip: Pork fillet is delicious and quite economical. If you have any left over, try cutting it into strips or thin slices and stir-fry with lots of fresh vegetables, serving with rice or noodles.)

name: Warm bananas and yoghurt
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 4 ripe bananas, peeled and sliced into diagonal chunks

steps: Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium-low heat and add the low-fat spread.

Add the banana pieces and fry gently for 2 minutes. Add the orange juice and cook for another 30 to 40 seconds. Sprinkle with the grated orange zest. (Tip: Take care not to overcook the bananas, or else they will go very mushy.)
Divide into bowls and top each portion with 1 tablespoon of low-fat Greek yoghurt.

name: Plum and peach grills
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Preheat the grill. Lightly toast the slices of bread on both sides. (Tip: Always try to choose wholemeal bread over white, as it provides the body with more fibre.)
Mix the soft cheese and vanilla extract together, then spread it on the toast. Top with the plums, and sliced peaches or nectarines.
Return to the grill for 3 to 4 minutes.
Top each portion with 1 tablespoon of the crème fraîche, sprinkle with a little ground nutmeg and serve. (Tip: Try to include fresh fruit for breakfast most days of the week.)

name: Classic vegetable soup
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 50g sugar snap peas or green beans, sliced

steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan. Add the onion, carrots, leek and celery, and fry gently for 3 or 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, beans, frozen peas and stock. Bring to the boil and add the pasta, herbs and pepper.
Lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes or until the pasta is cooked, stirring frequently to make sure the pasta doesn't stick.

Turn off the heat and leave to cool for a few minutes. Ladle into bowls and serve with a slice of wholemeal bread. (Tip: Chill any soup that you don't need and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months.)

name: Veg mix with cheese sauce
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 200g sugar snap peas or green beans, trimmed
6 spring onions, trimmed and finely chopped

steps: Put the cauliflower, broccoli and carrots in a steamer or colander positioned over a large saucepan of steadily boiling water. Steam for 5 to 6 minutes.

Add the sugar snap peas or green beans, and courgettes. Steam for about 5 more minutes, until the vegetables are cooked, yet still retain a little crunchiness. (Tip: Steaming is a healthier way of cooking fresh vegetables, so try to use this method more often. Alternatively, the vegetables can be cooked in a small amount of boiling water until tender.)
After the second batch of vegetables goes in, start making the sauce. Melt the low-fat spread in a saucepan and add the spring onions. Cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes to soften them.
Stir in the flour and cook gently over a low heat for a further minute, then remove from the heat.
Gradually add the milk, stirring until it is mixed in. Return to the heat and bring up to the boil, stirring constantly until the sauce thickens.
Add the cheese to the sauce and stir over a low heat until melted. Season with some pepper.
Pour the sauce over the vegetables and serve at once.

name: Fast chicken noodle soup
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 250g boneless, skinless roast chicken breasts, sliced

steps: Put the noodles into a heatproof bowl and cover them with boiling water. Leave to soak for 6 minutes.

Meanwhile, pour the stock into a large saucepan and bring to the boil. Add the vegetables and simmer for 5 minutes. (Tip: This is a great way to make the most of any fresh vegetables that need to be used up.)
Drain the noodles, then add them to the saucepan with the sliced chicken. Season with pepper.
Heat for 1 to 2 minutes, then ladle into bowls.
Serve each portion sprinkled with a few drops of soy sauce. (Tip: If you like things spicy, add a few fine slices of fresh red or green chilli, or a pinch of dried chilli flakes.)

name: Greek yoghurt and raspberry chill
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Preheat the grill. Sprinkle the porridge oats onto a baking sheet and spread them out evenly, then grill until they are light brown, about 2 or 3 minutes. Watch out to make sure they don't burn!
Once toasted, set the baking sheet aside and let the oats cool down.

While the oats cool, put half the raspberries into a mixing bowl. Use a fork or potato masher to squash them down slightly. Divide the rest of the whole raspberries between 4 serving glasses, saving 4 raspberries for decoration. (Tip: You can use forest fruits, strawberries or mixed summer berries (defrosted if frozen) instead of raspberries.)
Add the yoghurt and cooled oats to the bowl of crushed raspberries, and stir gently together. (Tip: Ordinary low-fat yoghurt works fine if you don't have any Greek-style.)
Spoon the raspberry mixture into the serving glasses and top each one with a whole raspberry. Cover and chill until you're ready to serve.

name: Haddock florentine
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Preheat the grill. Fill the kettle and boil it. Grill the haddock fillets, with the tomatoes at the side of the grill pan for 5 to 6 minutes until the fish is cooked (it should stop looking see-through and should flake easily). (Tip: For a treat, try salmon instead of haddock.)

Meanwhile, poach the eggs in gently simmering water for 4 to 5 minutes. Toast the slices of bread and spread them with reduced-fat spread. (Tip: Adding a shake of vinegar to the poaching water helps the eggs to keep together.)

Put the spinach in a large colander and slowly pour the kettleful of boiling water over the leaves to wilt them. Leave to drain for a few moments, then share between 4 warm plates. Arrange the fish on top, and place a poached egg onto each portion. (Tip: Serve with grilled mushrooms instead of spinach, if you prefer.)
Sprinkle with black pepper and serve with the tomatoes and toast.

name: Mummies' faces – Halloween
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 3 slices lean turkey ham, cut into thin strips
60g reduced-fat hard cheese, cut into thin strips
1 tablespoon sweetcorn (8 kernels are all you need)

steps: Preheat the grill.

Use a large biscuit cutter to cut out circles from the slices of bread. Toast these lightly on both sides. (Tip: If you don't have a large biscuit cutter, use an up-turned bowl to cut around for the bread circles.)

Spread 1 teaspoon of tomato purée onto each piece of toast, then sprinkle with herbs. Overlap the strips of turkey ham and cheese on top, to look like bandages, leaving a small space to put the "eyes". (Tip: Use thin slices of roast chicken or turkey instead of ham.)
Grill for 2 to 3 minutes to melt the cheese.
Put the halved tomatoes and sweetcorn on top of the faces, to look like "eyes". Eat while hot! (Tip: You could use white bread for this recipe, though wholemeal provides more fibre.)

name: Spider pies – Halloween
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 250g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
3 handfuls (or 200g) cauliflower, broken into small florets
300g uncooked chicken breasts, cut into small chunks

steps: Cook the potatoes in gently boiling water until tender.
Meanwhile, heat the vegetable oil in a non-stick frying pan and add the chicken, cooking for 3 to 4 minutes until sealed and browned.

Add the tomatoes, herbs, cauliflower, broccoli and stock. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until the vegetables are tender, adding an extra splash of water, if needed. (Tip: Use frozen broccoli and cauliflower instead, though cook for just 4 to 5 minutes.)

Stir the frozen mixed vegetables into the chicken mixture. Share between 4 large ramekin dishes or individual baking dishes and level the tops. Stand the dishes on a large baking sheet. (Tip: Try not to fill the dishes with too much liquid, or it could spill over the sides.)
Drain the potatoes and mash them with two tablespoons of the milk.

Preheat the oven to 200C (fan oven 180C, gas mark 6). Roll out the pastry on a lightly floured surface. For each spider pie, cut out 8 strips for the legs, and 1 small circle for the head. Arrange on the pies and brush with milk. Place a scoop of mashed potato on top of each pie for the spider's body. Sprinkle with poppy seeds. (Tip: You could make one giant spider pie in a round baking dish.)
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, then serve with the peas placed on the spiders' heads to look like eyes.

name: Eyeball meatballs – Halloween
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: Half a stock cube (reduced-salt vegetable or chicken stock), with 150ml boiled water

steps: Mix together the minced turkey with half the chopped onion, all the carrot and mixed herbs. Season with black pepper. (Tip: You can also use extra-lean pork mince or extra lean minced beef to make the meatballs.)
Form the mixture into 8 meatballs, using wet hands to prevent the mixture from sticking to them.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan, then add the meatballs. Fry gently, turning occasionally, until lightly browned. (Tip: Stir the meatballs gently so that they don't break up.)

Separately mix the stock cube in water, stiring until dissolved. Then add the remaining onion, tomatoes and the stock. Season with black pepper. Heat until boiling, then reduce the heat and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, cook the tagliatelle for 10 to 12 minutes in gently boiling water.

Share the tagliatelle between 4 serving plates and serve with the meatballs and sauce. Top each meatball with a mozzarella letting it melt for a few moments, then press the cherry tomatoes on top, to look like eyeballs. (Tip: Use small radishes, cut in half, instead of cherry tomatoes.)
Garnish with basil leaves, then serve.

name: Eyeball juice jellies – Halloween
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 250ml unsweetened apple and raspberry fruit juice

steps: If using lychees, peel off the skin and remove the stones. If using black grapes, split them, without cutting right through. Push a green grape into each lychee or black grape, then push a blueberry into each one, so that the fruits look like eyeballs. (Tip: You could use melon balls instead of green grapes for the "eyeballs".)
Put one "eyeball" into each of 4 serving glasses. Cover the remaining "eyeballs" and keep them chilled.
Pour 90ml of just-boiled water into a measuring jug and sprinkle in the powdered gelatine, stirring to mix it in. Leave for about 5 minutes, so that it dissolves into a clear liquid.

Mix the apple and raspberry juice and cold water into a large jug. Pour in the cooled gelatine liquid, stirring well. (Tip: Make sure you choose pure 100% fruit juice and not a "juice drink", which has added sugar. You could use 100% apple juice as an alternative.)
Share between the glasses and refrigerate until set. This should take about 2 to 3 hours.
Serve, decorated with the remaining "eyeballs". Scary!!

name: Fruity winter salad
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Put the cabbage into a large salad bowl. Add the red onion, carrot, apple, lemon juice and sultanas (raisins would also do). (Tip: If you like, add two satsumas, broken into segments, or use a can of mandarin oranges in natural juice, well drained.)
To make the dressing, put the soft cheese into a bowl and beat with a wooden spoon until softened. (Tip: For extra flavour, choose a lower-fat soft cheese with garlic and herbs.)
Add the yoghurt and mix together. Pour over the salad, season with some black pepper and toss to mix. Serve. (Tip: For a more filling lunch, try with a wholemeal bread roll.)

name: Chicken and tomato jacket potato
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 4 baking potatoes (each needs to be around 225g)

steps: Scrub the potatoes, then dry and prick each one several times with a sharp knife. (Tip: King Edward or Maris Piper potatoes would work best for this recipe.)

Microwave Method: Cook one potato (225g) for 6 minutes on full power (800W), turn halfway through cooking. Allow to stand for 1 to 2 minutes before serving. If cooking more than one potato at a time you need to increase the cooking time accordingly.
Oven Method: Rub a few drops of olive oil into the potato skin, place the potatoes in a pre-heated oven at 200C (fan 180C, gas mark 6). Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes, or until tender.

When the potatoes are almost ready, cut the chicken breasts into bite-size chunks, heat a non-stick frying pan and pan fry for about 6 to 8 minutes until lightly browned on both sides and cooked through. Add a pinch of dried oregano per person. (Tip: If you don't have dried oregano, rosemary or basil would also work well.)
Meanwhile, chop the tomatoes into chunks, discarding the seeds. When the chicken is cooked, mix together the chicken, tomatoes, spring onions and the pot of yoghurt. Add pesto if you wish.
Serve the jacket potatoes with a portion of the chicken mixture and enjoy.

name: Veggie spag bol
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 1 cube reduced-salt vegetable stock with 400ml boiled water

steps: Heat a large heavy-based saucepan. Add in the frozen vegetarian mince, onion, garlic, chilli, celery, carrot, aubergine and vegetable stock. Bring to the boil. (Tip: Substitute different vegetables, such as peppers, leeks, courgette or fine green beans.)

Add the tomatoes, dried herbs, tomato purée and mushrooms. Stir well. Simmer, partially covered, for 25 to 30 minutes, adding a little extra water if needed. Season with pepper. (Tip: Make a meat version with 300g extra-lean minced beef, dry-frying it in the saucepan until browned, then adding the rest of the ingredients.)

About 15 minutes before you want to eat, cook the spaghetti in plenty of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or according to pack instructions. Drain well, share between 4 warm plates and top with the Bolognese sauce. (Tip: Try reducing the quantity of spaghetti and pair it with cooked strips of carrot and courgette to add even more vegetables to it.)

name: Hot ham and tomato crumpets
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Preheat the grill and lightly toast the crumpets on both sides. (Tip: Use English muffins instead of crumpets - you'll need only 2, sliced in half.)

Spread each crumpet with 1 teaspoon of tomato purée, then top with two slices of wafer-thin ham. Arrange the sliced tomatoes on top. (Tip: Sprinkle a few mixed dried herbs over the tomato purée before adding the ham, if you like.)
Grill for 2 to 3 minutes. Serve at once.

name: Grilled plantain with fresh salsa
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: quarter of a cucumber, finely chopped

steps: Peel plantains by chopping both ends off and making a slit along the whole length of each plantain skin. Slide your thumb under the slit to loosen and remove the skin.
Cut each plantain in half and then cut each piece lengthwise. (You should have 8 pieces altogether).
Grill on a low heat turning occasionally for about 10 minutes or until cooked. (Plantains are soft inside but not sticky when cooked).
Meanwhile, make the salsa by mixing together the tomato, cucumber and spring onion. (Tip: Make a fruity salsa by substituting 2 chopped pineapple rings in natural juice for the tomato.)
Season with pepper, then serve with the warm plantain. (Tip: If you like things spicy, add a little finely chopped fresh red chili to the salsa, or use a pinch of chilli powder instead.)

name: Finger licking chicken pittas
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 150g skinless uncooked chicken (thigh or breast), cut into strips
You can use any chicken pieces you like. It doesn't need to be chicken breast, just make sure the skin and bones have been removed.
This recipe uses ready-made tikka masala paste. You only need a little and you can store the jar in the fridge for other recipes.

steps: Mix together the yoghurt, tomato puree and curry paste. Add the chicken and toss to coat. Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes to marinate. (Tip: You can also use turkey breast instead of chicken, if you prefer.)
Preheat a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the teaspoon of vegetable oil.
Put the marinated chicken pieces into the heated pan and stir-fry over a medium heat until cooked but still juicy (about 5 to 8 minutes).

Warm and split open the pitta breads and fill them with shredded lettuce. Add the cooked chicken, then serve with cherry tomatoes. (Tip: You can also serve with raw vegetable sticks and follow with an apple, orange or satsuma. This will add 2 extra portions of fruit and vegetables towards your 5 A Day!)

name: Courgette, rocket and ham pizza
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 2 thin and crispy pizza bases, 25cm wide
1 tablespoon fresh basil (or enough to garnish)

steps: Preheat the oven to 200C (fan oven 180C, gas mark 6).
Spread 2 tablespoons of tomato puree over each pizza base, then sprinkle the herbs on top.

Heat the olive oil in a non-stick frying pan and cook the onion and courgette for 5 to 6 minutes, until softened. Arrange evenly over the pizzas. (Tip: Use mushrooms instead of courgette, if you prefer.)
Transfer pizzas to the oven, baking them on the oven shelves for 10 to 12 minutes.

Remove from the oven and top with the rocket and torn-up slices of ham. Season with pepper and garnish with basil. Serve half a pizza each. (Tip: You can use thin slices of chicken or turkey as an alternative to ham as they are typically lower in fat. You can also use baby spinach leaves instead of rocket.)

name: Pronto pizza squares
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon (or enough to garnish) fresh basil
2 handfuls mixed salad leaves, to serve

steps: Preheat the grill to medium-high.
Place the wraps on a work surface and spread each one with 2 tablespoons of tomato puree, then sprinkle 1 teaspoon mixed herbs over the top of each one. Season with black pepper.

Arrange 2 sliced tomatoes over the top of each wrap, then sprinkle with cheese. (Tip: You can also add thinly sliced mushrooms or grated courgette to the top of the pizza before sprinkling with cheese.)
Grill each wrap, one-by-one, for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese melts and bubbles. (Tip: The base of your pizzas will be a bit floppy, so take care when transferring to plates.)
Serve with mixed salad leaves, garnished with olives and basil.

name: Super veggie soup
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Put the leeks, broccoli and potatoes into a large saucepan and add the stock. (Tip: You could use 2 medium onions instead of the leeks, if you prefer. This would also make the soup slightly cheaper.)
Heat until just boiling, and then turn the heat down. Cook over a low heat with the lid on for 15 to 20 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender.
Add the spinach and cook gently for another 2 to 3 minutes, until the leaves wilt down.

Blend the soup to a puree using a handheld stick blender, or transfer it to a food processor and whizz until smooth. Add the milk and reheat gently, seasoning with ground black pepper. (Tip: If you want to store the soup for later, cover, cool and refrigerate it. Use the soup within 3 days of making and re-heat thoroughly before eating.)
Serve, garnished with a few spinach leaves, if you like, and a slice of wholemeal bread.

name: Tortilla cheese turnovers
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 1 small avocado, peeled, pitted and finely chopped
1 teaspoon vegetable oil (for greasing the pan)
75g reduced fat mature Cheddar cheese, grated

steps: Make the salsa by mixing together the tomatoes, avocado and spring onions. Add a squeeze of lemon juice, then season the mixture with some pepper. (Tip: You can keep the filling really simple with just grated reduced fat cheese and chopped tomato, or whatever you have available!)
Grease a non-stick frying pan with a teaspoon of vegetable oil. Place the pan over a medium-high heat.

Add a tortilla to the pan and sprinkle a quarter of the cheese over the top. Heat for a few moments until the cheese starts to melt. (Tip: For a meat option, add little bits of cooked chicken or chopped ham to the tortillas. Add it just after the cheese but before the salsa.)
Sprinkle about 2 tablespoons of the salsa onto half of the tortilla. Fold in half using a wooden spatula or a fish slice, then cook for another few seconds to warm through.
Slide the cooked tortilla onto a serving plate and cut in half. Continue to cook the remaining tortillas in the same way.

name: Forest fruit milkshake
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 150g frozen summer berries, or forest fruits

steps: Slice the banana into a blender and add the frozen fruit (there's no need to thaw it first). (Tip: Try using frozen summer berries or frozen raspberries instead of forest fruits. Adding them to the blender while frozen makes an icy-cold milkshake.)
Add the low fat yoghurt and milk. Blend together for 15-20 seconds, then pour into 4 glasses. (Tip: If you don't have a traditional blender, use a hand-held stick blender instead.)
Serve and enjoy whilst cold!

name: Fruity French toast
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 200g defrosted frozen summer berries, or forest fruits

steps: Cut the slices of bread in half diagonally. (Tip: This recipe works well with slightly stale fruit bread, as the drier texture soaks up more of the liquid, so it's ideal for using up a 2 to 3 day-old loaf.)

In a large shallow dish, beat together the egg, milk and vanilla extract. Add the pieces of fruit bread and leave them for about 2 to 3 minutes, turning them over once so that each side is thoroughly soaked.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan and add the vegetable oil. Add the soaked bread and cook it gently for about 1 to 2 minutes until it has set and turned golden brown.
Turn over the pieces and cook them on the other side for another 1 to 2 minutes.

Share the bread between 4 warm plates. Slice the bananas over the top and serve with the thawed berries. (Tip: Instead of bananas or berries, try a sliced fresh mango or canned pineapple chunks or peaches packed in natural fruit juice.You can also serve with fresh strawberries, raspberries or blueberries when they come into season.)

name: Porridge with yoghurt and berries
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 100g defrosted frozen summer berries, or forest fruits

steps: Put the porridge oats and water into a non-stick saucepan. Heat and stir until boiling, then lower the heat and simmer gently, stirring often, for 5 minutes. (Tip: Remember to take the frozen fruit out of the freezer the night before so that it has thawed out in time for breakfast.)
Spoon the porridge into serving bowls and top each portion with 2 tablespoons of yoghurt. Spoon the berries on top and serve.

name: Raspberry and banana shakes
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Slice the bananas into a blender and add the frozen raspberries, yogurt, milk and vanilla extract. (Tip: Make a variation by using low-fat raspberry yoghurt and 150g strawberries instead of raspberries. When raspberries are in season, use them fresh instead of the frozen ones.)

Add to a blender and whizz together for a few seconds until smooth and blended, then pour into 6 glasses. Serve at once. (Tip: If you don't have a blender, you can use a hand-held stick blender, whizzing the ingredients together in a jug.)

name: Vanilla muesli milkshake
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Slice the banana into a blender and add the yoghurt, muesli, milk and vanilla extract. (Tip: If you don't have a blender, you can use a hand-held stick blender, whizzing the ingredients together in a jug.)
Blend everything together until smooth, then pour into 6 glasses. Serve at once. (Tip: To get the energy you need to start the day, you can serve this with a slice of wholemeal toast.)

name: English breakfast muffins
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Preheat the grill. Toast the muffins on the cut sides only. (Tip: Try using wholemeal soft rolls instead of English muffins, for a change.)

Meanwhile, beat the eggs and milk together. Heat the vegetable oil in a non-stick saucepan and add the eggs. Cook and stir to scramble them. (Tip: If you prefer, poach the eggs in gently simmering water for 3 to 4 minutes, until set, but still runny in the middle.)

Spread half the toasted muffins with reduced fat soft cheese and top with a slice of ham. Share the scrambled egg between the muffins, season with black pepper, then top with the remaining muffin halves. (Tip: For a vegetarian version, substitute the ham for sliced grilled tomatoes or sliced mushrooms, simmered in reduced-salt vegetable stock.)

name: Quorn and vegetable stir-fry
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram

ingredients.display: 4 spring onions, trimmed and finely chopped
1 pepper, any colour, deseeded and finely chopped

steps: Put the rice on to cook in a large saucepan of simmering water. Brown rice will take 30 to 35 minutes to cook; white rice will take 12 minutes.
When the rice has about 8 minutes left to cook, heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat.

Add the vegetables and frozen Quorn pieces. Stir-fry for 6 to 7 minutes, until the vegetables are cooked but still crunchy. (Tip: With any stir-fry, it's important to cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces so that they cook in the same amount of time.)
Add the Chinese 5-spice powder, soy sauce and sweet chilli sauce (if using) to the stir-fry. Season with some pepper and stir well. Share between 4 plates or bowls.
Drain the rice and serve with the stir-fry.

name: Mashed avocado cheese on toast
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Toast the slices of bread.

Meanwhile, peel, stone and mash the avocados with a fork. Spread the mixture evenly over the toast and arrange the tomatoes on top. Season with black pepper. (Tip: To check that an avocado is ripe, gently press the pointed end, it should 'give' a little.)
Sprinkle the cheese on top and grill for 2 to 3 minutes until melted and bubbling. (Tip: Grate the cheese finely to make it go further.)

name: Banana and sultana bread and butter pudding
attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
conversion_note: sodium computed from salt at 400 mg per gram
steps: Preheat the oven to 180C (fan oven 160C, gas mark 4)

Grease a 1.2 litre (2 pint) baking dish with a little reduced fat spread. Spread the rest over the bread, then cut each slice into 4 triangles. (Tip: This recipe is perfect for using bread that’s 2 to 3 days old. The drier bread soaks up more of the egg and milk mixture, giving a better texture.)
Arrange the bread slices in the dish with the sliced bananas and sultanas or raisins. (Tip: If you like, use chopped ready-to-eat dried apricots or dates instead of sultanas or raisins.)
Beat together the eggs, milk and vanilla extract. Stir in the sugar and allow a few minutes for it to dissolve. Pour the mixture over the bread, and let it soak in for 5 minutes.
Bake on the middle shelf of the oven for about 25 to 30 minutes, until set and golden brown.

name: 'Out of Salad Dressing' Salad Dressing
attribution: "'Out of Salad Dressing' Salad Dressing" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:'Out_of_Salad_Dressing'_Salad_Dressing, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Mix together lemon juice, Parmesan cheese, garlic salt, and mayonnaise until smooth.
Stir in milk, adjusting the amount or adding a little water, to make the dressing as thin or thick as you like.
Cover and refrigerate 8 hours, or overnight.

name: 1-2-3-4 Cake
attribution: "1-2-3-4 Cake" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:1-2-3-4_Cake, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 cups (450 g / 16 oz) white granulated sugar

steps: Preheat oven to 175 °C (350 °F)
Cream the butter and sugar together until fluffy.
Beat in the vanilla and eggs, one at a time, ensuring the batter is well mixed after each egg.
Gradually sift in the dry ingredients, alternating with small additions of the milk.
Transfer to a greased and floured baking pan.
Bake at 175 °C (350 °F), until a skewer inserted shows no moist crumbs.

name: 20-Ingredient Brownies
attribution: "20-Ingredient Brownies" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:20-Ingredient_Brownies, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cup (200 g / 7 oz) white granulated sugar
½ cup (60 g / 2 oz) dutch processed cocoa powder
½ cup (110 g / 4 oz) white granulated sugar
11 oz (330 ml / 1⅓ cups) heavy cream, heated

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Line a 33 x 23 cm (13 x 9-inch) baking pan with parchment.
Melt dark chocolate in microwave using 30-second bursts. Leave it to cool.
Beat the butter and sugars in a large bowl until combined.
Beat in the eggs, salt and vanilla, then beat in the melted chocolate.
Fold in the flour and cocoa, then the chopped chocolate.
Pour the mixture into the lined baking pan.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the topping by beating the cheeses in a medium-sized bowl until soft.
Beat in the sugar and vanilla, then beat in the egg and milk.
Take the brownie out of the oven after the 25 minutes of baking.
Pour the mixture over the brownie and bake for a further 30 minutes.
Take the brownie out of the oven and leave it to cool.
Make the ganache by mixing together the chocolate, hot cream and salt in a bowl until melted.
Pour the ganache over the brownie and chill in the fridge for at least a few hours until set.
Sprinkle the brownie with a light sprinkle of salt.
Trim the brownie and cut into 15 squares.

name: 20-Minute Beef Stroganoff
attribution: "20-Minute Beef Stroganoff" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:20-Minute_Beef_Stroganoff, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 8 oz wide egg noodles (figures are for yolk-free noodles)
1 package (17 oz) prepared beef tips with gravy
1 can (10.75 oz) condensed cream of mushroom soup (figures are for fat-free)
¼ teaspoon (or more to taste) mild or hot paprika
½ cup (250 ml) sour cream (figures are for reduced-fat)
¼ cup (125 g) finely-chopped fresh parsley

steps: Prepare noodles according to package directions and drain.
As the noodles are boiling, warm oil in very deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add mushrooms and onions and cook until onion is soft, about 3 minutes.
Add beef tips, milk, and mushroom soup.
Add salt and pepper to taste and stir well.
Reduce heat to simmer and stir in garlic, paprika, and sour cream.
Simmer lightly, without letting it boil (that will curdle it).
When noodles are finished and drained, serve with noodles on serving plate or individual plates, with sauce over it.
Garnish with parsley.

name: 8 Desserts in 1 Pan
attribution: "8 Desserts in 1 Pan" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:8_Desserts_in_1_Pan, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ½ cup (90 g) light brown sugar
½ cup (90 g) golden superfine sugar
2 cups (240 g) all-purpose flour, more if needed
1 small bag (approximately ⅓ cup / 40 g) M&Ms
1 ea. (approximately 260 g) Bramley or green cooking apple
¼ cup (45 g) light brown sugar
13×18-inch (33×46 cm) baking sheet with short walls

steps: Combine the butter and sugar in a mixing bowl and cream until fluffy and very light.
Add the egg and vanilla, and beat in.
Fold in the flour, salt and baking soda. This should form a soft dough that is not sticky to the touch.
Mix in the chocolate chips, folding well to distribute.
Divide the dough equally into two bowls.
In one bowl, mix in the M&Ms.
Set aside both the doughs.
Combine the brownie mix with egg, oil and water. This should form a very thick batter that is only slightly softer than cookie dough. Set aside.
Line a baking sheet with paper towels.
Core and roughly chop the apple and transfer to the prepared baking sheet and fold the towel in half. Set aside for 1 hour.
Combine the sugar, cinnamon and flour in a bowl.
Add the apple, and mix using your hands to coat. Set aside.
Combine the egg and sugar in a mixing bowl by whisking until smooth.
Mix in other ingredients until smooth. Set aside.
Cream the butter and sugar until soft and fluffy.
Combine in other ingredients until smooth. Set aside.
Combine all ingredients until smooth. Set aside.
Preheat the oven to 150°C (302°F).

Cut baking paper into a rectangle the size of your baking pan. Use a pencil and ruler to divide the paper into 8 equal sections—halved length-wise and quartered width-wise, as in the layout diagram. Annotate the sections as described in the diagram.
Grease the baking pan and line with the annotated paper.
Shape both cookie doughs into rectangles measuring 4½×6½ inches (11.5×16.5 cm). Align the doughs with their respective sections.

Break the graham crackers into smaller rectangles. Place them, on edge, along the borders of the s'mores section, pressing them against the cookie doughs for support. You are essentially making walls to hold in the s'mores section.
Place two graham crackers on the bottom of the s'mores section to create the base. Distribute the chocolate on top, then sprinkle with the marshmallows.

Spread brownie batter over its respective section. It should be stiff enough to hold its shape. Using your wet hands or a spatula, gently press the right wall of batter to correctly align it with the right wall of the M&Ms cookie dough.

If necessary, press the pastry dough sheets together so that they are big enough to cover both the pumpkin pie and apple pie sections of the pan. Press the dough over the right side of pan so that it covers these two sections and goes up three of the walls. Trim away any overhang as necessary.

Use a long strip of dough, stood on edge, to create a wall between the pie section and the rest of the pan. Press to seal it with the existing dough. In a similar fashion, use another strip of pastry to create a wall between the pumpkin and apple sections so the fillings don't combine. Press to seal.
Spread the apple pie and pumpkin pie fillings in their respective sections.
Create graham cracker walls around the cheesecake section, and line the bottom with graham crackers. Spread the cheesecake filling over top.
Spread the banana bread batter in the last remaining section.
Bake for an hour in the preheated oven. Transfer to a wire rack and leave to cool completely.
Slice into 32 squares (4 along the longer sides, 8 along the smaller sides).

name: Aadun (Nigerian Corn Flour with Palm Oil)
attribution: "Aadun (Nigerian Corn Flour with Palm Oil)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Aadun_(Nigerian_Corn_Flour_with_Palm_Oil), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine the corn flour, palm oil, chili pepper, and salt in a bowl.
Leave the mixture to sit for 2–3 hours.
Shape the mixture as desired, and serve with drinks.
wikibooks_categories: CS1 maint: numeric names: authors list

name: Abacha
attribution: "Abacha" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Abacha, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Soak the abacha in warm water for 5–10 minutes, or until softened.
Drain the abacha thoroughly and set aside.
Dissolve the potash in a small quantity of water and strain to remove any sediment.
Pour the palm oil into a mixing bowl. Gradually add the strained potash solution while stirring continuously until the oil thickens and turns yellow.
Add the ground crayfish, pepper, salt, and crushed seasoning cubes. Mix well to form a smooth sauce.
Add the softened abacha to the sauce and stir until evenly coated.
Add the ugba, sliced garden eggs, and sliced utazi leaves. Mix thoroughly.
Add the fish or stockfish, if using, and stir gently to combine.
Adjust the seasoning to taste.
Serve immediately as a main dish or side dish.

name: Abacha Mmiri (Soaked Cassava Flakes)
attribution: "Abacha Mmiri (Soaked Cassava Flakes)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Abacha_Mmiri_(Soaked_Cassava_Flakes), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Peel the cassava, then cut into slices 1 cm thick. Rinse well.
Boil the cassava in a large pot of water until cooked through.
Soak the cooked cassava in fresh water overnight. The next day, drain away any remaining water and rinse the cassava well.
Season the cassava to taste with the salt.
Serve the cassava with the coconut, palm kernel, and roasted groundnut.

name: Abula (Nigerian Three Stews)
attribution: "Abula (Nigerian Three Stews)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Abula_(Nigerian_Three_Stews), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 large pieces of meat, cut into pieces

steps: Soak the beans in water overnight. Remove and discard the skins.
Boil the beans in fresh water until very soft. Drain well.
Blend the beans to a purée using a blender. Set aside.
Boil the meat in a pot of water with onions and spices. Remove the meat and set aside.
Heat a small amount of palm oil in a pot. Add the blended beans, crayfish, salt, boiled meat, and dryfish. Cook until the fish is softened.
Boil the ewedu for about 15 minutes.
Soften with potash, then add a pinch of salt and stock cube.
Blend the ewedu mixture until smooth, and stir in the locust beans.
Reduce the heat, and allow to simmer.
Blend the pepper and tomato together until smooth.
Heat a small amount of oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the blended mixture, and cook until it loses the raw flavor.
Serve the pepper sauce in one dish with the gbegiri and ewedu.

name: Acevichada Sauce
attribution: "Acevichada Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Acevichada_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Pour the lime juice into a bowl.
Add the salt and test the flavor. It should be neither too salty nor too acidic. If needed, rectify by adding more salt or lime juice to find the right balance.
Add the onions, chiles, garlic, cilantro, hondashi, black pepper, and togarashi.
Cover with plastic wrap and reserve in the fridge for at least 15 minutes, so the flavors from the vegetables and spices can integrate into the lime juice.
Crack the eggs into a blender, and start blending at low speed.
While running the blender, very gradually start adding 250 ml of the oil until the mixture thickens to a mayonnaise consistency. Use more or less oil as needed.
Pause the blender, pour your leche de tigre into the mix, and start blending again.
Gradually stream in the remaining 125 ml oil until the mix thickens again.
Turn off the blender and taste for salt. If needed, add a little more salt, and blend again until it suits your taste.

name: Achicha Ede
attribution: "Achicha Ede" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Achicha_Ede, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Mortar and pestle (optional, for crushing cocoyam if not pre-processed)

steps: Soak the dried cocoyam flakes (achicha) in warm water for about 10–20 minutes or until they become soft. Drain and set aside.
If using stockfish or dried fish, soak in hot water to soften, then clean thoroughly and cook until tender. Set aside.
Heat palm oil in a large pot over medium heat until slightly warm (do not bleach the oil).
Add chopped onions and fry lightly until fragrant.
Add ground crayfish, pepper, and salt, and stir well to combine with the oil.
Add the cooked fish or stockfish and mix gently to allow the flavors to blend.
Pour in a small amount of water or stock and bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
Add the softened achicha (cocoyam flakes) gradually while stirring to ensure even mixing.
Add ugba (oil bean seeds) and stir carefully so the flakes do not break down too much.
Reduce heat and allow the mixture to simmer for 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Once everything is well combined and heated through, remove from heat.
Serve warm, preferably with palm oil–rich garnishing or extra ugba on top if desired.

name: Achicha Ji
attribution: "Achicha Ji" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Achicha_Ji, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Peel the yam and cut into medium cubes. Wash and set aside.
Soak the dried cocoyam flakes (achicha) in warm water until soft, then drain.
If using fish or stockfish, soak, clean, and cook until tender.
Place yam in a pot, add water, and boil until the yam becomes soft.
Lightly mash some of the yam while leaving some chunks intact to form a thick base.
Add palm oil and stir to combine with the yam.
Add chopped onions, pepper, crayfish, and salt. Stir well.
Add the cooked fish or stockfish and mix gently.
Add the softened achicha and stir carefully to avoid breaking it too much.
Add ugba and mix until evenly distributed.
Simmer on low heat for 10–15 minutes, allowing all flavours to combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Remove from heat and serve warm.

name: Acorn Crusted Salmon
attribution: "Acorn Crusted Salmon" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Acorn_Crusted_Salmon, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Use a food processor, blender or other method (meat tenderizer, etc.) to pulverize the acorns into a fine meal. If desired, toast the acorn meal for 5-7 minutes at 375°F/190°C/gas mark 5. Transfer the acorn meal to a dish.
Place the egg whites in a shallow dish. Coat each salmon fillet in egg white.
Coat each fillet with the acorn meal.
Transfer coated fillets to a slightly greased or non-stick baking sheet.
Bake for 10-15 minutes in a 425°F/220°C/gas mark 7 oven, or until the fish is flaky when pulled apart with a fork.
Serve.
Heat a few tablespoons of oil in in a frying pan over medium-high heat. When the oil is hot, add the coated salmon fillets.
Pan fry the salmon for 2–3 minutes per side, depending on the thickness of the fillet, until fish is flaky when pulled apart with a fork.
Serve.

name: Acorn Squash with Orange Marmalade
attribution: "Acorn Squash with Orange Marmalade" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Acorn_Squash_with_Orange_Marmalade, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F (204°C).
Remove seeds and strings from squash halves.
Cut a small piece off outside of each half to make a flat space on which the half can stand level.
Place halves in a shallow pan or casserole in ¼ inch (6 mm) water with insides facing down. Bake for 35 minutes.
Combine marmalade and butter in a small bowl.
Remove squash from oven, and invert in pan or dish. Salt lightly.
Spread marmalade and butter mixture on edges of squash, allowing excess to run into center.
Place under broiler for 5 minutes or until lightly browned.

name: Adobo Sauce
attribution: "Adobo Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Adobo_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 12 chipotle peppers or smoked, dried jalapeño peppers (most co-ops can get these for you, or try the specialty produce section of your grocery store)
⅓ cup (80 ml) apple cider vinegar

steps: Combine all ingredients in a heavy saucepan. Cook over a very low heat for 1–2 hours until the chiles are very soft and the liquid has been reduced to about 1 cup. Alternatively, cook in a slow cooker overnight.
Beat with a mortar and pestle, or put in blender to puree for a thick sauce.

name: Adult Macaroni and Cheese
attribution: "Adult Macaroni and Cheese" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Adult_Macaroni_and_Cheese, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ½ tsp (2.5 ml) kosher salt, plus more for the water
½ cup (60 g / 2.1 oz) grated Fontina
½ cup (60 g / 2.1 oz) grated Gruyere
½ cup (150 g / 5.3 oz) mascarpone cheese
½ cup (150 g / 5.3 oz) cream cheese
1¼ sticks (150 g / 5.3 oz) unsalted butter, divided

steps: In a gallon (~3.8 L) of salted boiling water, cook macaroni to al dente. Strain into a colander and rinse with cold water.
While pasta is cooking, in a heavy saucepan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat. Once bubbling ceases, whisk in flour and cook, whisking continuously, until blonde.
Add remaining ingredients except butter. Once cheese is melted and sauce is smooth, add 1 tbsp butter, whisking continuously until melted. Repeat until all butter has been used.
Gently fold in macaroni and serve warm.

name: Afang Soup
attribution: "Afang Soup" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Afang_Soup, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Wash and prepare all vegetables, meat, and fish.
Cook the meat and stockfish with seasoning until tender.
Add water or stock and bring to a boil.
Add palm oil and allow it to dissolve into the soup.
Add ground crayfish, pepper, and salt.
Add the waterleaf and cook until slightly softened.
Add the ground afang (okazi) leaves and stir well.
Simmer for 10–15 minutes until well combined and thickened.
Adjust seasoning and allow to simmer briefly.
Serve hot with swallow of choice.

name: Afghan Bread
attribution: "Afghan Bread" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Afghan_Bread, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Mix ½ cup water, yeast, and sugar. Let it sit for 10 minutes until foamy.

Place flour in a mixing bowl and sprinkle in the salt. Make a well, then add oil and yeast mixture. Stir in add small amounts of the remaining water until it forms a soft dough that can be moulded. Knead for 5 mins. Cover with paper and let rise for 1½ hours.
Mix together the egg yolk and 1 tablespoon of water to make egg wash. Set aside.
Divide dough into eight parts and roll each into a ball. Roll each bread into an oval shape 20 cm long and 5 cm thick.
Make lines in top of dough. Brush on egg wash, and sprinkle with black cumin seeds.
Bake in a preheated 350°F (175°C) oven for 25 mins. Total cooking time is around 2½ hours.

name: Agar Jelly
attribution: "Agar Jelly" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Agar_Jelly, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Put agar, sugar, and water in a saucepan and bring to boil.
Take off heat, and drain some of the water.
When cool, add in milk and almond extract.
Pour mixture into tin.
When completely cool, chill in the refrigerator for about 15 minutes until set.
Cut almond jelly into cubes.
Serve with fruit cocktail and syrup in a glass bowl.

name: Agbalumo Smoothie
attribution: "Agbalumo Smoothie" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Agbalumo_Smoothie, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Peel the skin off the star apples and remove the seeds.
Transfer the peeled fruit to the blender.
Begin blending the fruit, adding water to get your desired consistency.
Sweeten to taste with honey or sugar.
Strain the smoothie through a sieve, and serve.

name: Agbugbu (Nigerian Pigeon Pea and Yam Porridge)
attribution: "Agbugbu (Nigerian Pigeon Pea and Yam Porridge)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Agbugbu_(Nigerian_Pigeon_Pea_and_Yam_Porridge), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Yam, cut into small pieces and rinsed

steps: Pick any dirt or debris out of the pigeon peas, then wash them and soak in water overnight.
Drain away the soaking water.
Cover the pigeon peas in fresh water, and bring to a boil. Cook until tender, then drain.
Boil the yam in water until tender, then drain.
Fry the onions, ground crayfish, ground pepper in a pan with palm oil.
Add the drained yam and pigeon peas, and stir gently.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve.

name: Ager Soup
attribution: "Ager Soup" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Ager_Soup, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Scrape off the white flaky skin of the ager stalk. Pound gently for a few minutes to remove the ager pulp.
Squeeze the pulp in a small amount of water to extract the slippery juice. Sieve this product to separate the juice from the fibres.
Heat a little water in a pot, and add the ager juice.
Add the palm oil, blended pepper, blended tomato, beef, and fish. Cook for few minutes, stirring continuously until an elastic consistency is achieved.
Add nune, maggi cubes, and salt to taste.
Serve with swallows as desired.

name: Agidi (Nigerian Cornstarch Swallow)
attribution: "Agidi (Nigerian Cornstarch Swallow)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Agidi_(Nigerian_Cornstarch_Swallow), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Gradually mix the water into the corn starch until you get a smooth, lump-free mixture. If desired, add a little sugar to taste.
Transfer the mixture to a pot, and stir continuously over medium-low heat until it thickens to a smooth, custard-like consistency.
Add a little water around the sides of the pot, cover, and simmer for about 10 minutes
Stir well, and test for doneness by placing a small portion in cold water; if it sets firmly after cooling, the agidi is ready.
Transfer the mixture into containers or wrap in leaves, then allow it to cool completely and set before serving.

name: Agnolotti Pasta Soup (Agnolotti in Brodo)
attribution: "Agnolotti Pasta Soup (Agnolotti in Brodo)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Agnolotti_Pasta_Soup_(Agnolotti_in_Brodo), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 250 grams (8–9 ounces) of agnolotti or other small ravioli-type pasta
½ litre (2 cups) of chicken broth (canned or homemade) or ½ litre of water and 2 good-quality chicken stock cubes
1 dash (you decide how big or small) of sweet sherry

steps: Bring the chicken broth to a rolling boil. If using water and chicken stock cubes, bring the water to a boil, add the stock cubes and let dissolve.
Add the agnolotti and cook according to the instructions on the package.
Add the cream, freshly-ground black pepper, and chopped parsley about 2 minutes before the end of the cooking, and turn down the heat.
Add the dash of sherry just before serving. If serving to children, dish out their portions first, then add the sherry for the grown-ups.
Let stand for a few minutes to marry the flavors, then serve, sprinkled with grated Parmesan cheese and enjoy.

name: Air Fried Zucchini
attribution: "Air Fried Zucchini" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Air_Fried_Zucchini, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Dice zucchini into medium-sized squares.
Transfer zucchini to a bowl, and add olive oil to your preference. A few tablespoons is a good starting point.
Add the season salt, garlic powder, and onion powder. Toss to coat all the zucchini well.
Put in air fryer, and cook for 8 minutes at about 205 °C (400 °F) or until crispy.

name: Ají de Gallina (Peruvian Chili Chicken)
attribution: "Ají de Gallina (Peruvian Chili Chicken)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Aj%C3%AD_de_Gallina_(Peruvian_Chili_Chicken), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 3 hot yellow South American chilis (seeds and filaments removed): Adjust quantity for individual taste.
1.6 kg (3.5 lbs) boiled rice (flavored with chopped garlic and salt)

steps: Boil chicken in salted water together with the stock cube. Remove bones and break into bite size pieces, keeping the resulting chicken stock.
In a saucepan, heat oil and sauté the onion, garlic, and finely chopped chili peppers and add salt and pepper. Fry this until the onions are cooked and golden.
Soak the bread in two cups of the stock from the boiled chicken and place in a blender for a couple of minutes and then add the resulting liquid to the saucepan.
Cook slowly for ten minutes. Cook slowly, stirring to thicken.

While the Ají de Gallina is cooking slowly, boil the rice: first fry the garlic for a couple of seconds, then add the rice and the salt, then add the water. When the water starts to boil, let the rice cook in a closed pot very slowly for about 20 minutes or until the water has completely evaporated (hint: to cook "peruvian" rice: cook a cup of rice in two cups of water).

Back to the Ají de Gallina: add the chopped pecans, grated cheese, and chicken pieces. Cook until it has a thick creamy texture. About five minutes before serving, add the evaporated milk and continue cooking on low heat.
Serve over the boiled rice and garnish with halved potatoes, eggs quartered lengthwise, and olives.

name: Akamu (Nigerian Pudding)
attribution: "Akamu (Nigerian Pudding)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Akamu_(Nigerian_Pudding), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Fill a large basin halfway with the akamu lumps. Because akamu rises during preparation, use a bowl large enough to hold the meal in its elevated position. If in doubt, use a large bowl and allow plenty of time.
Crush the ogi lumps with a spoon into very little pieces. Mix in small amounts of cold water until the mixture is smooth and has the consistency of evaporated milk.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil.

Stir the mixture thoroughly just before the water boils, as some akamu may have accumulated at the bottom of the basin. Once the water has reached a boil, carefully but steadily stir it into the akamu mixture. Stop stirring as soon as the mixture starts to set, and reduce the flow of water you're pouring to the bare minimum until the akamu has entirely set.
Thoroughly whisk the mixture. Add additional water as desired if the mixture is too thick.
Stir in evaporated milk and a pinch of sugar to taste.

name: Alabama White Sauce
attribution: "Alabama White Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Alabama_White_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
