name: Italian Rice Pilaf
attribution: "Italian Rice Pilaf" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Italian_Rice_Pilaf, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium high heat. Add rice and onion and cook until rice is golden.

Meanwhile, combine remaining ingredients. Once rice has toasted, remove from pot and add mixture. Bring to a boil and add rice. Cook, stirring occasionally, 30 minutes or until rice is desired tenderness.
Serve warm with a steak, a glass of red wine, and maybe a vegetable sauté.

name: Italian Rice Pudding
attribution: "Italian Rice Pudding" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Italian_Rice_Pudding, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Bring water to a boil, then add rice, salt, and butter.
Cover, lower heat to simmer, and cook for 20 minutes.
Place rice in upper part of double boiler with half and half, sugar, cinnamon stick, and lemon peel.
Bring to boil over direct heat.
Place over simmering water in double boiler and cook for 45 minutes.
Remove cinnamon stick and lemon peel.
Pour rice mixture into a 2-quart (1.9 L) casserole and allow to cool.
Sprinkle with cinnamon powder.

name: Italian Rice with Wild Mushrooms
attribution: "Italian Rice with Wild Mushrooms" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Italian_Rice_with_Wild_Mushrooms, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 4 ounces (commercial) wild mushrooms, sliced and sautéed

steps: Bring the stock to a simmer before you begin. It's important that the temperature is as high as possible, without letting the stock boil. The surface of the stock should just be moving a little.
Sauté the shallots in olive oil until soft.
Add the rice, stirring for 3–5 minutes, until coated with oil.
Pour in wine and about ½ cup of the hot broth and continue stirring.
Keep adding liquid as necessary and stir for an additional 15 minutes, keeping the rice creamy.
Remove from heat and add Parmesan cheese, mushrooms, and truffle oil.
Serve immediately.

name: Italian Seasoning
attribution: "Italian Seasoning" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Italian_Seasoning, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Mix together well or pulse about a minute in a food processor.
Store in an airtight container.

name: Italian Soup with Poultry Quenelles
attribution: "Italian Soup with Poultry Quenelles" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Italian_Soup_with_Poultry_Quenelles, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Pound the poultry breast. Mix in ground rice, egg yolk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Pass the mixture through a sieve.
Form the mixture into quenelles.
Simmer the quenelles in the stock to make a soup.

name: Italian Tricolor Soup
attribution: "Italian Tricolor Soup" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Italian_Tricolor_Soup, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Make a savoury custard and divide it into three parts. Leave one white, color one red with tomato, and color the last one green with spinach.
Put a layer of each colored custard in a buttered saucepan, and cook for about 10 minutes until solidified.
Cut the solidified custards into dice.
Put the colored custard pieces into a soup tureen and pour broth over top.

name: Ivorian Grilled Chicken
attribution: "Ivorian Grilled Chicken" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Ivorian_Grilled_Chicken, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 3 tablespoons chile powder or 20 fresh puréed red habanero chillies

steps: Combine the garlic, pepper, chili powder, mustard, and bouillon cubes. Pour the mixture over the chicken and massage it very well. Let rest for about 20 minutes while you prepare the grill.
Place the chicken on the grill, turning it regularly until each piece become golden brown.
When it is done to your taste, serve with any complimentary side such as Ivorian tomato sauce or Ivorian salad and enjoy.

name: Jahnun (Yemenite Layered Pastry)
attribution: "Jahnun (Yemenite Layered Pastry)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jahnun_(Yemenite_Layered_Pastry), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2–3 tbsp white granulated sugar (or to taste)
200 g butter, soft margarine, or shortening

steps: Combine the flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt. Make a well in the center.
Add some of the water to the well, and mix with your hands. Gradually knead in the rest of the water, then continue kneading for 15 minutes. The dough should not be too soft or sticky.

Tear off a piece of dough the size of your fist. Flatten and roll it out on your work surface, then shape again into a ball. Repeat this step for the rest of the dough, then brush all the balls with a thin coating of oil.
Allow the dough to rest for about 1–2 hours, until they have sunken slightly.
Roll and stretch each ball out on a greased surface until it is very thin. Try to make the dough as thin as possible without it tearing.

Spread some soft butter over the whole surface of the flattened dough. Make a triangular fold lengthwise, like a shirt fold: fold one-third of the dough toward the middle then fold the other side. Make a small fold up and down, and start rolling (with greased hands) from the bottom to the top, like folding a sleeping bag. You should be left with an elongated, slightly fat rolled jachnun. Repeat this shaping step for all the dough balls.
Preheat oven to 212 F. Line a pot with slices of bread or pita so that it does not become overly dry while baking in the oven.

Place the unbaked jachnun into a cookie bag, with each bag holding a single layer of jachnun. This prevents loss of moisture. Stack the jachnun in the pot, with 2–3 rows stacked one on top of the other in a criss-crossed fashion (horizontally and vertically).
Cover the pot with the lid, and bake in the preheated oven for 6–10 hours.
Serve with hard-boiled eggs and tomato salsa, with a little zhug over the paste.

name: Jal-jeera (Cumin Mango Lemonade)
attribution: "Jal-jeera (Cumin Mango Lemonade)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jal-jeera_(Cumin_Mango_Lemonade), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ¼ tsp ground mint leaves (grind to paste)

steps: Combine all the ingredients in a glass.
Serve.

name: Jalapeno Eggs
attribution: "Jalapeno Eggs" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jalapeno_Eggs, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Pickled jalapenos (the kind you have on tacos)

steps: Chop and fry the onions, then set aside.
Warm the tomato beans over medium heat.
Fry the bacon and set it aside. Reserve the bacon grease.
Slice the bread and apply margarine generously.
Heat a frying pan with the bacon grease.
Start frying 2 eggs. Do not crack the yolk.
When the eggs are nearly done, draw aside the egg white so the yolk is clear.
Chop the pickled jalapeños and spread them over the eggs. Add some of the pickle juice as well.
Sprinkle some cheese over the eggs.
Put a lid over the frying pan and let the cheese melt.
Serve the eggs on the bread with the onions, tomato beans, and bacon.

name: Jalebi (Fritters in Syrup)
attribution: "Jalebi (Fritters in Syrup)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jalebi_(Fritters_in_Syrup), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 3 cups of vegetable oil/ghee for deep frying

steps: Mix up the batter ingredients until smooth.
Let the batter sit unrefrigerated and uncovered overnight (about 12 hours).
Mix the sugar, water, and cream of tartar for the syrup.
Stir the syrup over moderate heat until the sugar is dissolved.
Put on high heat and boil for 5 minutes.
Let the syrup cool, and stir in the rosewater. Use food coloring to tint it light orange.
Put the vegetable oil in a wide wok-like dish, and heat to about 350°F (175°C).
Put the batter into a pastry bag with about a ¼ inch opening. If it is too dry to squeeze out, mix in a bit of water.
Squeeze the batter into the oil, making a couple of figure-eight shapes and loops on top of each other. The shape should be about 3 inches on its longest side.
Fry each jalebi until golden brown. Remove, let the oil drain off, then soak in syrup for a minute.
Serve.

name: Jam Roly-Poly
attribution: "Jam Roly-Poly" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jam_Roly-Poly, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 250 g (1 cup or 8 oz) self-rising flour
125 g (½ cup or 4 oz) shredded suet

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F or Gas Mark 6).
Sift the flour into a bowl with the salt. Add the suet and sufficient water to create a soft but not sticky dough.
Turn on to a floured board and roll out to a rectangle about 20×30 cm (8×12 inches).
Brush the pastry with the warmed jam, leaving a 1 cm (½ inch) border all around.
Fold in this border and brush with milk. With the short side towards you, roll up the pastry loosely and seal the ends well.
Place on a greased baking sheet, with the sealed edge underneath. Brush with the beaten egg and sprinkle with caster sugar.
Bake in the oven for 35–40 minutes until golden brown.
Remove from the oven, sprinkle on a little more sugar and serve hot with home-made English custard.

name: Jamaican Banana Fritters
attribution: "Jamaican Banana Fritters" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jamaican_Banana_Fritters, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Peel the bananas and mash them in a bowl until runny.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan at medium heat.
Add the sugar, milk, vanilla, salt, and flour to the bananas and mix until approximately the consistency of pancake batter or a bit thinner.
Drop tablespoons of the mixture into the heated oil, and fry until edges are firm, then flip to cook other side until golden brown.
Drain on a towel and serve hot.

name: Jamaican Chicken Fingers with Honey-Mustard Sauce
attribution: "Jamaican Chicken Fingers with Honey-Mustard Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jamaican_Chicken_Fingers_with_Honey-Mustard_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 pound (500 g) boneless, skinless chicken breast
3 cups (750 ml) cornflakes, crushed to make 1 ½ cups
½ cup (125 ml) honey-mustard salad dressing

steps: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Trim fat from chicken.
Cut chicken lengthwise into ¾ inch-wide strips.
In shallow dish whisk together egg whites and honey.
In another shallow dish combine cereal and jerk seasoning.
Dip chicken pieces in egg mixture and then roll dipped pieces in cereal mixture.
Place the cereal-coated pieces in a single layer on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake at 450°F for 11–13 minutes or until tender and no longer pink.
While baking, in small bowl stir together salad dressing and lime peel.
Serve chicken and mango slices with salad dressing mixture.

name: Jamaican Curry Chicken with Bullga
attribution: "Jamaican Curry Chicken with Bullga" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jamaican_Curry_Chicken_with_Bullga, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Just over ½ cup olive oil

steps: Cut chicken in equally-sized pieces.
Rinse the chicken in lime juice.
Combine the chicken with the green onions, onions, chile peppers, curry powder, salt, and pepper. Let marinate 5–10 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a pot. Add the chicken mixture, and cook for 30–60 minutes.
Serve with bulla cakes.

name: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
attribution: "Jamaican Jerk Chicken" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jamaican_Jerk_Chicken, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine rum and mustard, and rub all over chicken.
Combine remaining ingredients and rub all over chicken. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour, but it is better to marinate overnight.
Place chicken on a greased, preheated charcoal grill. Cook, turning constantly until internal temperature reaches 165°F. Remove and let rest for 10 minutes.
Serve.

name: Jamaican Jerk Spice I
attribution: "Jamaican Jerk Spice I" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jamaican_Jerk_Spice_I, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine all ingredients together.
Store in an airtight container.

name: Jamaican Jerk Spice II
attribution: "Jamaican Jerk Spice II" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jamaican_Jerk_Spice_II, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine all ingredients.
Store in an airtight container.

name: Jamaican Sorrel Soda
attribution: "Jamaican Sorrel Soda" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jamaican_Sorrel_Soda, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 3 hibiscus (roselle) tea bags or 3 tsp (15 ml) dried hibiscus
6 ea. ¼ in (0.67 cm) cubes of ginger (optional)

steps: Combine the water, hibiscus, and ginger in a pot. Boil for about 15 minutes.
Remove and discard the hibiscus and ginger.
Stir the sugar into the liquid, and simmer until you have about 5 oz (150 ml) syrup.
Remove from the heat and let cool.
To make the finished soda, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of sparkling water.

name: Jambalaya I
attribution: "Jambalaya I" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jambalaya_I, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 14.5 ounces (411 g) canned tomatoes, diced or torn apart
2 cups cooked and chopped turkey or chicken
1 small can of sliced mushrooms (optional), drained

steps: Mix the salt, savory, basil, thyme, and cumin together, then grind them to a powder.
Prepare the canned tomatoes: tear them up, remove the stem ends, remove the seeds, etc. Keep the juice.
Heat a wide pan with a lid. Lightly fry the celery in the butter. Soften the celery but do not brown it.
Add everything to the pan. You can add the basil, meat, and mushrooms later if you prefer.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for about 20 minutes. The rice will absorb the liquid.
Discard the bay leaf.

name: Jambalaya II
attribution: "Jambalaya II" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jambalaya_II, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cup (240 ml) chopped green bell pepper
½ cup (120 ml) diced cooked ham
2 cans (29 ounces / 800 g total) stewed tomatoes
1 cup (240 ml) uncooked long grain rice
1 ½ tsp salt, or to taste

steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet; add chicken and paprika, then brown on all sides.
Remove chicken from skillet.
Add onion, green bell pepper, celery, and garlic. Sauté over low heat until onion is tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in ham, tomatoes, chicken broth, rice, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Add chicken and turn to coat with sauce. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.

name: Jambons
attribution: "Jambons" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jambons, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 150 g grated cheese (Dubliner Cheese recommended, can be substituted)

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Melt butter over medium heat and add flour. Cook for 5 minutes and begin adding milk gradually until the mixture thickens.
Cut your pre-prepared puff pastry into squares and spoon a generous amount of the mixture onto each square. Sprinkle some ham and grated cheese on top.
Fold the corners of the puff pastry so that they meet in the centre, forming a panier feuilleté (puff pastry basket) shape.
Beat the egg and brush it over each sealed panier feuilleté.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden brown.

name: Jerk Lobster
attribution: "Jerk Lobster" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jerk_Lobster, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 tsp lemon juice or lime juice
½ tsp Jamaican pickapeppa sauce or 3 drops of Jamaican hot pepper sauce (optional)

steps: Thinly slice the scallions.
Melt the butter in a small skillet.
Lightly sauté the scallions until golden.
Add the lemon juice.
Add Jamaica pickapeppa sauce or hot pepper sauce (optional, depending on your taste).
Let it simmer for about 1 minute, then set aside.
Remove the membrane from the lobster tails.
Use a sharp knife to split the lobster tail in half lengthwise.
Brush butter sauce onto each tail.
Using the same brush, spread the jerk sauce over the tails, especially on the exposed meat. Set oven to broil.
Put the lobster tails in oven on the meat side for 4 minutes, turn, and cook the shell side for 2 minutes.
If you want a more smoked taste, cook for 2 minutes on each side in the oven, then place on a barbecue grill for 3 minutes. You may need to add more jerk sauce if using a grill.
Serve with Jamaican festival and/or bammy. You can also serve with Jamaican hardo bread.

name: Jersey Breakfast Dog
attribution: "Jersey Breakfast Dog" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jersey_Breakfast_Dog, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Preheat deep fryer to 355°F.
Wrap bacon around the hot dog, securing at each end with a toothpick.
When oil reaches 355°F, lower wrapped hot dog into fryer.
Heat frying pan and fry one egg.
Place cooked egg on a small plate.
Open bun and place onto frying pan on low heat or in toaster oven to lightly toast.
When bacon is firm and crispy, remove hot dog from oil.
Place slice of cheese onto egg and microwave for 7-10 seconds.
Place egg and cheese on to bun.
Remove toothpicks from hot dog, and add to bun.
Add condiments and serve.

name: Jollof Rice
attribution: "Jollof Rice" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Jollof_Rice, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Wash the rice thoroughly and set aside.
Blend the tomatoes, peppers, and one onion until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot.
Chop the remaining onion and fry until softened.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended tomato mixture and cook until the sauce thickens.
Season the sauce with seasoning cubes, curry powder, thyme, and salt.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a boil.
Add the rice and stir to combine.
Cover the pot and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
If necessary, add a small amount of water during cooking.
Fluff the rice with a fork and serve hot.

name: Ka'ak (Savory Ring-Shaped Biscuit)
attribution: "Ka'ak (Savory Ring-Shaped Biscuit)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Ka'ak_(Savory_Ring-Shaped_Biscuit), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ½ cup vegetable oil (preferably canola oil)
1 tbsp baking powder or dried yeast
10 g dried marjoram, za'atar or oregano (optional)
¾ tsp ground Mahaleb cherry (Prunus mahaleb) kernels (optional)

steps: Combine water, oil and soft margarine (or butter) in bowl.
Mix together flour, baking powder (or dried yeast), brown sugar, salt, and spices.
Mix dry ingredients with wet ingredients (except egg yolks) until you get a dough.
Let dough mixture rest for 30 minutes until it reaches its proper consistency.
Cut dough into half. Roll each half into a coil with your hands. You should now have 2 pieces.
Cut each coil in half, and again roll out each coil into a smaller coil with one's hands. You should now have 4 pieces.
Cut each coil in half, and again roll out each coil into a smaller coil with one's hands. You should now have 8 pieces.
Cut each coil at angles into 4 equal pieces. You should now have 32 pieces
Pinch together the ends of each coil so that it forms a ring. Place on a baking sheet, and let sit until the dough rises.
Brush each dough ring with egg yolk.
Bake in a preheated oven at a low heat (212–338°F / 100–170°C) until they begin to emit vapors. Then, remove from the oven.

name: Kabab Barg (Persian Grilled Meat)
attribution: "Kabab Barg (Persian Grilled Meat)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kabab_Barg_(Persian_Grilled_Meat), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 kg lamb, cut into 1 x 5 cm pieces

steps: Combine the olive oil, onions, garlic, saffron, salt, and pepper to make the marinade.
Toss the lamb pieces with the marinade. Cover, and marinate overnight in the refrigerator.
Thread the lamb onto metal skewers.
Brush the lamb with the marinade. Grill for 5–10 minutes on each side over an open fire.

name: Kachumbari
attribution: "Kachumbari" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kachumbari, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Gently toss together all the ingredients in a mixing bowl until well-distributed.
Allow the salad to rest for 5–10 minutes.
Taste the salad and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Serve fresh.

name: Kal Kals (Sweet Curled Fritters)
attribution: "Kal Kals (Sweet Curled Fritters)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kal_Kals_(Sweet_Curled_Fritters), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine flour, egg, baking powder, powdered sugar, and vanilla to make a moist but not sticky dough.
Flatten teaspoon-sized balls of dough on the back of a fork (preferably with rounded tines) and roll off, forming small snail-shell-like curls.
Deep fry in hot oil (~350°F/180°C), six at a time, until golden brown.
Roll in more powdered sugar while still hot to coat.

name: Kanachi (Armenian Herb Salad)
attribution: "Kanachi (Armenian Herb Salad)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kanachi_(Armenian_Herb_Salad), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Remove extra stem endings, yellow leaves, and damaged parts from all herbs and wash them thoroughly. Drain.
Remove roots from green onions and radishes and majority of radish leaves (leaving only the younger ones). Wash them thoroughly and drain.
Mix them up or arrange them on a plate.
Eat raw and enjoy!

name: Kanafeh (Egyptian Sweet Cheese Pastry)
attribution: "Kanafeh (Egyptian Sweet Cheese Pastry)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kanafeh_(Egyptian_Sweet_Cheese_Pastry), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Adjust the oven rack to the lower-middle position and preheat it to 400°F (204°C).
In a medium bowl, combine the mozzarella cheese and cream cheese, then set it aside.
Slice the kadaif pastry crosswise into ¼–½-inch lengths and transfer it to a large bowl.

Pour the melted butter over the pastry in the bowl. Using your hands, gently toss the pastry with the butter, ensuring that all the shreds are evenly coated. Continue this process for about 5 minutes.
Transfer half of the coated pastry to the skillet, spreading it evenly along the bottom of the pan.
Spread the cheese mixture evenly over the first layer of pastry, leaving a ½-inch border along the rim.
Layer the remaining pastry over the cheese layer, firmly pressing it down.
Bake the prepared pastry in the preheated oven until it turns deeply golden brown, which takes about 40 minutes.
While the pastry bakes, prepare the syrup. In a saucepan, combine the sugar, lemon juice, and 1 cup of water.
Simmer the syrup until it reaches a temperature of 234°F (112°C), or until a small amount dropped into ice water forms a soft ball consistency. Remove from the heat and cool.
When the pastry is ready, add the rose water and orange blossom water to the syrup.
Invert the cooked pastry onto a serving platter and drizzle it with the syrup. Sprinkle chopped walnuts over the top and serve immediately.

name: Kansas City Barbecue Sauce
attribution: "Kansas City Barbecue Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kansas_City_Barbecue_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine all ingredients in a large saucepan, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Cook, stirring often for 15 minutes.
Cool, and keep refrigerated in a nonreactive container for up to 2 months.

name: Kari Ayam (Indonesian Chicken Curry)
attribution: "Kari Ayam (Indonesian Chicken Curry)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kari_Ayam_(Indonesian_Chicken_Curry), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 lb (450 g) boneless, skinless chicken parts
5 Asian shallots, sliced (or ½ cup chopped onions)
½ tsp turmeric root, ground or grated
½ tsp galangal root, ground or grated

steps: Wash chicken parts.
In a food processor or mortar and pestle, grind the garlic, ginger, kimiri nuts, turmeric, galangal, hot chilies, and terasi into a paste (bumbu).
In a wok or skillet, cook the paste over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the chicken parts to the wok, and brown them.
Add the shallots, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and salam leaves to the wok, and sauté for another minute.
Add the coconut milk and bring to a light boil.
Simmer on low heat for 10 minutes.

name: Kashkaval Pane (Bulgarian Fried Cheese)
attribution: "Kashkaval Pane (Bulgarian Fried Cheese)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kashkaval_Pane_(Bulgarian_Fried_Cheese), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Flour seasoned with salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps: Cut the yellow cheese into slices about ½ inch thick. Wet in water. Gently pat off any excess moisture with paper towels.
Heat the oil in a pot until a small piece of bread sizzles as soon as it is dropped in.
Beat the eggs in a shallow bowl, while the oil is heating.
Spread some seasoned flour on a plate and some bread crumbs on another plate.

Press the yellow cheese slices into the flour, coating them evenly with a thin layer of flour, shaking off any excess flour. Dip them into the egg, then into the bread crumbs, then once more into the egg, then again into the bread crumbs, covering the whole slice.
Fry immediately in the hot oil until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot, garnished with parsley. Enjoy!

name: Kashmiri Pulao
attribution: "Kashmiri Pulao" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kashmiri_Pulao, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cinnamon tree leaf (or substitute 2 bay leaves)
½ kilogram basmati or other long-grained rice, cooked and drained
100 grams dried dates, pitted and sliced thin

steps: Heat ghee or butter in a large wide pan or wok.
Add the cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon tree leaf.
Add the chopped onion, and fry until it just begins to turn brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and chillies and fry for about 1 minute before tossing in all of the dried fruits and nuts.
Add salt to taste.
Turn the flame down to low.
Soak the strands of saffron in milk, mixing until the milk turns orange.
Pour the cooked rice into the pan and sprinkle the saffron-milk on top.
Stir very carefully so as not to break or mash up the rice grains, mixing the flavourings and saffron colour in uniformly and heating the rice.
Mix in dried fruits and nuts.
Add more ghee according to your preference.
Serve with a gravy such as the basic tomato gravy.

name: Kasnocken (Austrian Cheese Dumplings)
attribution: "Kasnocken (Austrian Cheese Dumplings)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kasnocken_(Austrian_Cheese_Dumplings), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 120 g fatty cheese plus 120 g low-fat cheese OR 250 g Pinzgauer Bierkäse cheese

steps: Mix flour, eggs, water, and salt carefully to get a dough; it should neither be stiff nor too soft.
Pass the dough through a special press for dumplings into boiling, salted water.
Boil the small dumplings for about 3 minutes, then drain and rinse them with cold water.
Melt the butter in a pan, add the dumplings, and season them with salt and pepper.
Gradually add the grated cheese and stir vigorously.
When all of the cheese has melted, heat butter in another pan, add the onion rings, and fry them until they become golden brown.
Top the dumplings with the onion rings and chives.

name: Kawlata (Maltese Vegetable and Pork Soup)
attribution: "Kawlata (Maltese Vegetable and Pork Soup)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kawlata_(Maltese_Vegetable_and_Pork_Soup), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 4 shoulder-cut pork chops (ideally left attached in one piece and separated only after cooking)
1 piece (300 g) fresh pork belly, salt-cured gammon, or smoked bacon
1 ham hock or a pig's trotter (not boned)
1 whole medium cabbage, cut into medium chunks
2 large potatoes, cut into medium chunks
1 large slice of red-fleshed pumpkin (qargħa hamra; optional), cut into medium chunks
1 large slice of yellow-fleshed pumpkin (qargħa Torka; optional), cut into medium chunks
½ ea. medium cauliflower (optional), cut into medium chunks
1–2 tbsp tomato paste, diluted with a little water
A few sprigs of flat-leaf parsley, chopped

steps: Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil, and scald the hock or trotter in it for 10 minutes.
Remove the hock or trotter, discard the water, refill with fresh water and bring to the boil again.
Place the hock or trotter in the boiling water with the other meats you are using, turn heat down, and cook a few minutes, skimming scum from the surface.
When there is no more scum forming, remove the meats from the water. Reserve both the cooking water and all the meats.
In a pot over medium heat, soften and wilt the onion in the olive oil without letting it brown.
Add the cabbage, potatoes, kohlrabi, pumpkin, cauliflower, carrots, and celery leaves. Season with salt and pepper, cover, and sweat together on low heat for 5–6 minutes
Add the tomato paste and reserved meats.

Add some of the water in which you boiled the meats (the quantity depends on whether you want a one-dish stew or a two course meal, see below). Simmer over moderately low heat until the meats are tender.
Five minutes from the end of cooking time, taste and adjust for seasoning, then add the chopped flat leaf parsley.

name: Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
attribution: "Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kedgeree_(Rice_and_Smoked_Fish), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1–2 cups Basmati or long-grain white rice (see notes)
2–4 cups decent quality low-sodium chicken stock
3 medium shallots or 1 medium onion, chopped fairly fine
As much garlic as you can handle, minced or put through a garlic press
6 hard boiled eggs, chopped fairly fine
At least 3 tsp of prepared English mustard (1½ tsp of dry mustard)
Enough finely-chopped parsley or cilantro to add interest and colour

steps: Cook the rice in one and a half the amount of chicken stock with the bay leaf. When it is done and keeping warm, discard the bay leaf, fluff the rice with chopsticks, and place the raw smoked haddock slab on top. Close the lid and let the haddock steam on warm for 15 minutes.
Remove the haddock, and flake with forks to get rid of every last trace of bone. Place the haddock back with the rice.
Sauté the shallots in excess butter until light brown. Add the garlic, and cook for 1 minute more, making sure to not brown it. Transfer mixture to the rice.

Add the eggs, mustard, parsley, pepper, curry powder, and enough cream to make everything just slightly creamy. Mix it all up, gently and thoroughly (chopsticks are perfect for this). Season with salt to taste.
Serve immediately or later—it keeps well.

name: Kerala Pachadi (Coconut Mango Condiment)
attribution: "Kerala Pachadi (Coconut Mango Condiment)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kerala_Pachadi_(Coconut_Mango_Condiment), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Peel and cut the mango into small pieces. Mix with salt and set aside.
Grind the coconut with water and 2 of the dried chilies until well-blended.
Add the coconut-chili mixture to the mango, and mix well.
Heat oil in a kadai; add the mustard and remaining dried chilies, and fry.
Pour into the mango coconut mixture, and cook briefly.
Serve with plain rice.

name: Keralan Prawns
attribution: "Keralan Prawns" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Keralan_Prawns, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Kudampuli (Malabar tamarind) to your preferred sourness (can be substituted with lime juice)
20 pieces chipped coconut kernel (thin slices approximately 2 cm long each)

steps: Remove the prawn tails and heads.
Cook the prawns in water with ginger, salt, curry leaves, green chillies, kudampuli and coconut. Leave a little water in the vessel at the end of cooking.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the turmeric, chili powder and coriander powder in it until they turn brown.
Add the onion and sauté until wilted.
Add the cooked shrimp and simmer, stirring, until it reaches a semi-dry consistency.

name: Keralan Vegetable Stew
attribution: "Keralan Vegetable Stew" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Keralan_Vegetable_Stew, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1½ cups boiled vegetables (carrots, green beans, potatoes, peas, etc.)
1 very small piece of ginger, chopped
1 Tbsp flour or rice flour or cornstarch

steps: Pour ¾ cup of water into the grated coconut. Squeeze out the milk through a strainer. Set aside; this is first milk.
Pour ½ cup of water into the same coconut and squeeze out the second milk. Keep this aside as well.
In a large pan, heat oil and add the cloves, cinnamon, and cardamom.
Add the chopped onion, ginger, chillies and curry leaves. Fry until the onion is slightly browned.
Add the boiled vegetables and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the second milk and boil for about 5–7 minutes.
Add salt. Dissolve the maida/rice flour in a little water and add it to the sauce.
When it boils again, add the first milk.
Remove from the flame when it starts to boil once more.
Season with the pepper, mustard, and shallot.

name: Kesari (South Indian Semolina Pudding)
attribution: "Kesari (South Indian Semolina Pudding)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kesari_(South_Indian_Semolina_Pudding), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ¾ cup jaggery or granulated sugar

steps: Bring the water to a boil.
Soak the saffron in the warm milk.
Lightly toast the semolina in a deep-bottom pot. When the semolina is golden brown, add the boiling water, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Add the sugar, pineapple, and cardamom to the mix while stirring.
Keep stirring well, and cook on low heat until the mixture comes together well.
Heat the ghee or butter in a separate pan, add cashews, and fry to golden brown.
Add raisins and fry for a few seconds until they swell up.
Add the nuts and raisins to the kesari.
Add the saffron milk along with the saffron, and mix well.
Serve hot.

name: Key Lime Meringue Pie
attribution: "Key Lime Meringue Pie" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Key_Lime_Meringue_Pie, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 fully-baked 9-inch (25 cm / 9 oz) graham cracker or pastry pie shell
1 can (14 oz / 400 g) sweetened condensed milk
½ cup fresh Key lime juice

steps: Separate egg whites from egg yolks. Make sure there is no trace of yolk in the whites.
Beat the sweetened condensed milk, lime juice, and egg yolks in a small mixing bowl.
Pour the mixture into the baked pie shell. Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 8 minutes.
While baking filling, whip egg whites in a large, clean mixer bowl on high speed until soft peaks form. Gradually beat in the sugar until meringue forms hard peaks.
Spoon the meringue over the top of the hot pie and use a spoon to form peaks.
Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 10–15 minutes, or until meringue begins to brown.

name: Khaman Dhokla (Steamed Gram Bread)
attribution: "Khaman Dhokla (Steamed Gram Bread)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Khaman_Dhokla_(Steamed_Gram_Bread), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 tsp ginger and green chile paste

steps: Grease a 125 mm (5-inch) diameter tin with oil.
Combine the gram flour, semolina, sugar, ginger chili paste, and salt in a bowl. Mix in just enough water to get a thick batter.
Add the fruit salt and 2 tsp water. Wait for the bubbles to form, then mix gently to distribute the leavening through the batter.
Pour the batter immediately into the prepared tin, and swirl the tin clockwise in order to spread the batter in an even layer.
Immediately place the tin in a steamer. Cover and steam for 12–15 minutes, or until the dhoklas are cooked.
Remove from the steamer and set aside to cool slightly.
Heat the oil in small pan, and add the mustard seeds.
When the seeds start crackling, add the sesame seeds, green chillies, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Mix well and sauté on a medium flame for a few minutes, stirring continuously.
Remove mixture from the flame, then add 2 tbsp of water and mix well.
Unmold the dhokla and cut into equal pieces. Spread the topping mixture on top, and serve immediately, garnished with coriander.

name: Khao Pad (Thai Fried Rice)
attribution: "Khao Pad (Thai Fried Rice)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Khao_Pad_(Thai_Fried_Rice), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cup cooked meat (e.g. shrimp, pork, chicken, etc.)

steps: Heat up a frying pan or wok and add the oil, then the minced garlic. Stir fry until fragrant.
Add the eggs, and stir fry the eggs until cooked.
Add the rice and stir fry.
Season with fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar, then continue frying until the rice is crumbly.
Add meat, pepper, and spring onions. Stir again until heated through, then transfer to a serving dish.

name: Khao Pad Gai (Thai Chicken Fried Rice)
attribution: "Khao Pad Gai (Thai Chicken Fried Rice)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Khao_Pad_Gai_(Thai_Chicken_Fried_Rice), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 large chicken breast, sliced in thin strips
4 cups (900 g) cooked Thai jasmine rice, refrigerated overnight
½ yellow onion, chopped into strips
¾ roma tomato, cut into strips
¾ cup (180 g) cilantro, finely chopped
3 slices cucumber, peeled (note: can run fork down all sides lightly if desired)

steps: Make sure that all of the ingredients are prepared and set aside in small bowls by the stove.
Add about 4 Tbsp peanut oil to the wok, and turn the flame to high heat.
When the oil is almost smoking, add the chicken strips and push around vigorously with a wok spoon or spatula.
When the chicken seems as if it is starting to brown, push it up the side of the wok and crack the eggs into the wok.
Stir the eggs around a bit. When almost fully scrambled, mix in the chicken and stir around for 30 seconds more.
Push the eggs/chicken to the side, add some more oil, and throw in the tomato and onion. Stir-fry for about 5 minutes. They will not look done, but in the end, they will be fine.
Add the cold cooked rice and mix it all in.
Turn the heat to low, then add a few splashes of fish sauce and soy sauce to taste.
Add sugar, salt, MSG, a splash of vinegar, and chili sauce if wanted. Lastly, add the fried garlic on top. Stir it all in and turn off the heat.
On a large platter, arrange the garnishes on a lettuce leaf, and plate the fried rice next to it.
Eat the garnishes with the fried rice.

name: Khara Pongal (Rice and Mung Bean Porridge)
attribution: "Khara Pongal (Rice and Mung Bean Porridge)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Khara_Pongal_(Rice_and_Mung_Bean_Porridge), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Cook the rice and dhal together with turmeric powder in a pot or pressure cooker until mushy.
Heat a little ghee in a large pan and brown the cashew nuts. Remove them from the pan.
Add the rest of the ghee and the oil and heat.
Throw in all of the spices, starting with the mustard seed and finishing with the cashew nuts.
Mix in the rice and dhal, warming through. If it is too thick, add a little water.
Add salt and extra ghee to taste. You can also add some grated coconut at the end.

name: Kheer (Rice Pudding)
attribution: "Kheer (Rice Pudding)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kheer_(Rice_Pudding), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 250 ml (1 cup) long grain white rice

steps: Bring the milk to a boil. Stir regularly to prevent scorching.
Add rice and simmer slowly until thick (about 20 minutes).
Stir in the sugar, sultanas, and the ground cardamom seeds. Cook for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in the almonds and rosewater, and cover until ready to serve.

name: Khichdi (South Asian Rice and Lentils)
attribution: "Khichdi (South Asian Rice and Lentils)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Khichdi_(South_Asian_Rice_and_Lentils), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 teacup dal (e.g. moong dhal, arhar dal or masoor dal or combination thereof)

steps: Wash rice and lentils and soak them for 10–15 minutes in water.
Add salt and turmeric powder.
Pressure cook with 3–4 cups of water.
After the first whistle, reduce the heat and cook for 4–5 more minutes.
Allow to cool. Serve with ghee or buttermilk.

name: Khubz Muluwah (Yemenite Layered Flatbread)
attribution: "Khubz Muluwah (Yemenite Layered Flatbread)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Khubz_Muluwah_(Yemenite_Layered_Flatbread), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Mix together flour and salt in large bowl.
Gradually mix in the water to make a dough with a uniform consistency.
Sprinkle with water, and let dough rest for 45 minutes.
Begin to work the dough again, stretching it and folding it over onto itself. Cover and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Place on cutting board, and cut into two equal parts. Shape each piece into a ball.
Use your hands to flatten the dough on a floured surface. Use a rolling pin to roll it into a very thin round.
Brush the surface dough with ghee, and sprinkle lightly with black cumin.
Cut flattened dough into elongated strips and fold one end, lengthwise, over itself. Baste with ghee (or butter) and sprinkle with black cumin.
Repeat process with other ball of dough.

After both balls of dough have been flattened out and each one folded over itself in repeated folds (with added ghee and black cumin on each fold), combine the two elongated dough portions, placing one on top of the other.
Begin to roll up the dough from one end, just as one would do to a sleeping bag. After completely rolled-up, turn it so that it will lay down upon its side (with the coiled rings facing upward).
Once rolled-up in this fashion, cover and allow the dough to rest 15 minutes.

Take up dough and brush it with ghee (or butter) and sprinkle a little black cumin over its surface. Once again, roll-out the dough with a rolling pin (maintaining its round shape). Dust the flat surface with flour if needed, to prevent its sticking.
Take up the flattened dough and place on heated griddle. Add ghee once more and cook until golden on each side.

name: Khus Khus Halwa
attribution: "Khus Khus Halwa" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Khus_Khus_Halwa, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 medium-sized mango, peeled and fleshed removed

steps: Blend together the mango flesh, sugar, milk, vanilla, and cinnamon powder until smooth.
Add a bit of maida to the batter and whisk it well.
Dip the bread slices in the batter and fry them in a oiled pan until brown on both sides.
Serve hot.

name: Kid-Friendly Pasta
attribution: "Kid-Friendly Pasta" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kid-Friendly_Pasta, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Add spaghetti and carrots to the boiling water, and cook for 4 minutes.
Add green beans, and cook for another 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the tomato sauce.
Drain the spaghetti and the vegetables, then mix it with the heated sauce.
Add a pinch of salt if needed.
Serve.

name: Kid-Friendly Pizza
attribution: "Kid-Friendly Pizza" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kid-Friendly_Pizza, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ½ cup cubed cooked chicken breast (optional)

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Spread the tomato sauce on the pizza shell.
Top it with half of the shredded cheese.
Add the chicken and red pepper on top of the pizza crust in whatever design you want. Have fun with it!
Sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top.
Bake it for 10–12 minutes.

name: Kilishi (Nigerian Beef Jerky)
attribution: "Kilishi (Nigerian Beef Jerky)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kilishi_(Nigerian_Beef_Jerky), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 250–300 g beef, trimmed of fat and sliced very thin

steps: Rub salt on both sides of the beef slices and let sit for 10 minutes.
Lay the slices flat on a baking sheet. Bake in a preheated oven at 250°C (482°F) for 15 minutes, turning every 5 minutes.
Pound or blend the ginger and garlic into a paste. In a bowl, mix the paste with the stock cube, cloves, cayenne seeds, suya spice, and a few tablespoons of water to form a marinade.
Rub the marinade onto the partially baked meat slices, coating them well.
Return the slices to the oven and bake for another 10–15 minutes, flipping occasionally until fully dry and slightly crispy.
Remove from the oven and let cool before serving or storing.

name: Killer Queso Dip
attribution: "Killer Queso Dip" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Killer_Queso_Dip, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 10 oz (280 g) canned tomatoes stewed with green chiles (e.g. Rotel brand)
Tortilla chips or fritos for serving

steps: Brown sausage in saucepan and drain grease.
Add cubed cheese, diced tomatoes, and diced chilies.
Heat over low, stirring until cheese is melted and ingredients are well blended.
Brown sausage in a skillet and drain grease.
In a slow cooker, melt cheese with tomatoes and chilies, stirring.
Add browned sausage. Stir until well melted and mixed.

name: Kiwi and Asian Pear in Lemon Dressing
attribution: "Kiwi and Asian Pear in Lemon Dressing" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kiwi_and_Asian_Pear_in_Lemon_Dressing, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Finely-grated fresh peel of 1 small lemon
2 kiwifruit, peeled, sliced, and cut into thin strips
1 crisp Asian pear, sliced, and cut into thin strips (crisp Anjou pear may be substituted)
½ yellow or red bell pepper, cut into thin strips
½ European cucumber, halved, seeded, and cut into thin strips

steps: Whisk the lemon dressing ingredients together in a serving bowl, and set aside.
Add the fruit to the bowl of lemon dressing. Toss, cover, and chill for about an hour.

name: Knoephla (Small Flour Dumplings)
attribution: "Knoephla (Small Flour Dumplings)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Knoephla_(Small_Flour_Dumplings), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ½ cup (250 ml) milk or water

steps: In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, egg, and then the milk or water. Mix to form a firm dough that is not sticky. Add a bit more flour if needed to keep dough from being sticky or a bit more liquid if too dry.
Roll pieces of dough between the hands to the length of a pencil (6 in / 15 cm). Snip off small pieces with a knife or scissors.
Use the knoephla as specified in your given recipe.

name: Knoephla Soup
attribution: "Knoephla Soup" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Knoephla_Soup, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Knoephla yielded from 2 cups of flour

steps: Melt the butter in a large soup kettle over medium heat. Add the add the onion, and sauté until onions are tender.

Add the water and soup base. Bring to a rapid boil over high heat. Add the knoephla by dropping them into the boiling broth. Stir until they all float to the top, and cook until the dumplings are soft.
Add the potatoes, then simmer over medium heat until dumplings and potatoes are done throughout.
Remove from heat. Add the cream, then season with parsley as well as salt and pepper to taste.

name: Koko da Kosai (Fermented Corn Porridge and Bean Fritters)
attribution: "Koko da Kosai (Fermented Corn Porridge and Bean Fritters)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Koko_da_Kosai_(Fermented_Corn_Porridge_and_Bean_Fritters), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cup millet grains (also known as jiƙo)
¼ teaspoon black pepper or chile powder (optional)
1 cup black-eyed peas (wake), soaked overnight and peeled
1–2 fresh chili peppers, chopped (or to taste)

steps: Place the millet in a large bowl, and cover with a large volume of cool, clean water. Let soak for 1–2 days to ferment slightly, changing the water daily to avoid spoilage.
Rinse and drain the millet, then use a blender or other suitable tool to grind it to a smooth paste with the 2 cups of water.
Using a fine sieve or cheesecloth, strain the paste to remove the chaff. Discard the chaff and keep the liquid starch mixture (called koko base).

Transfer the koko base, potash, ginger, and cloves to a pot over medium heat. Stirring continuously to avoid lumps, cook until the mixture thickens into a smooth porridge. Remove from heat when it reaches a creamy consistency.
If desired, add sugar or milk to taste before serving.
Cover the black-eyed peas with cool water, and soak them for 4–12 hours. Drain and peel the skins from the beans.
Blend the peeled beans, onion, and just enough water to get a smooth and thick purée. Do not make the mixture too watery.
Stir in salt and chili pepper.
In a deep frying pan, heat enough vegetable oil for deep frying over medium-high heat.
Use a spoon to gently scoop small portions of the batter into hot oil. Fry until golden brown on both sides (about 2–3 minutes per side).
Remove from the oil using a slotted spoon and place on paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve the kosai with the finished koko.

name: Komle (Norwegian Potato Dumplings)
attribution: "Komle (Norwegian Potato Dumplings)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Komle_(Norwegian_Potato_Dumplings), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Chop the potatoes in a food processor.
Squeeze the potato mass to discard the water.
Mix the potatoes with the flour, and let the dough rest for 10 minutes.
Shape the dough into big round balls, and fill them with pieces of the salted pork.
Boil the balls in beef stock for about 15–20 minutes.

name: Korean Shortribs
attribution: "Korean Shortribs" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Korean_Shortribs, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Process all ingredients except meat in a blender until smooth. Pour into a gallon size zip-top bag, and add shortribs.
Toss to coat the meat in the marinade, and refrigerate overnight. Note that this flavors but does not tenderize the meat.
Preheat grill to 225–300°F. Add shortribs and cover. Cook 5 hours or until meat falls right off the bone and is extremely tender. Serve immediately.

name: Koshary (Egyptian Pasta Salad with Rice and Lentils)
attribution: "Koshary (Egyptian Pasta Salad with Rice and Lentils)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Koshary_(Egyptian_Pasta_Salad_with_Rice_and_Lentils), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon ground black pepper, more to taste
1 teaspoon white wine vinegar, more to taste

steps: If using dried chickpeas and lentils, soak them in water overnight.
Boil the rice, chickpeas, and lentils until tender. Cook the macaroni until al dente. Drain all.
In a sealable container (e.g. a tupperware), layer the rice, the lentils, and the macaroni, and then the chickpeas. This is the koshari base.
Sauté the diced onions in olive oil until crisp. Drain off the excess oil if desired, and reserve for garnish.
Mix the tomato paste and water in a saucepan. Put on medium high heat, and stir in the cumin, black pepper and vinegar.
Heat the sauce until most of the liquid evaporates.
Add warm or hot water, and simmer it on low heat. Using a hand blender to increase consistency is optional.

name: Kubaneh (Yemenite Pull-Apart Bread)
attribution: "Kubaneh (Yemenite Pull-Apart Bread)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kubaneh_(Yemenite_Pull-Apart_Bread), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2½–3 cups lukewarm water (or enough for kneading dough)
3 cups white, all-purpose wheat flour (optional: try using some sorghum flour)
2 tbsp vegetable oil or other fat

steps: Dissolve salt in lukewarm water.
Sprinkle yeast over lukewarm water and add sugar. Leave for 10 minutes until yeast is foamy.
Add yeast mixture to flour, and knead to form a dough.
After kneading the dough, allow it to sit 10 minutes until it begins to rise.

Repeat process: turn it and knead it again and let sit 10 minutes until it rises. Repeat this process 3 or 4 times until dough rises to the top of the kneading bowl and one is left with a uniform texture and consistency.
Grease the baking pot with the vegetable oil.
Divide dough into smaller pieces (8–10 round pieces).
Place all dough pieces in pot, one after the other; compacted together. Fill to one-third the capacity of baking pot and cover tightly with lid.
Preheat oven to 225–280°F (107–138°C). Bake bread for 1 hour at the higher temperature or 3 hours at the lower temperature. It should be golden brown.
Turn bread out onto a plate, turn bread upside down, and restore to baking pot.
Cover pot with lid and bake another hour; or reduce oven temperature to 200 F and bake overnight. If desired, remove from oven and afterwards return it only close to the Sabbath.
Serve hot with clarified butter, usually also with tomato salsa mixed with chopped coriander.

name: Kuddi (Spiced Yogurt Sauce)
attribution: "Kuddi (Spiced Yogurt Sauce)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kuddi_(Spiced_Yogurt_Sauce), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine the yogurt, chickpea flour, sugar, salt, grated ginger, and chopped green chilli.
Heat and bring to a boil with continuous stirring.
Taste and add more sugar or salt as needed. It should be sour, salty, and sweet.
Fry the jeera seeds in butter, and mix them into the kuddi.
Serve.

name: Kugelis (Lithuanian Baked Potato Pudding)
attribution: "Kugelis (Lithuanian Baked Potato Pudding)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kugelis_(Lithuanian_Baked_Potato_Pudding), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 5 lb potatoes, peeled and grated (or ground with a food processor)
1 lb bacon, fried and crumbled (reserve about ¼ cup drippings)

steps: Combine the grated potatoes and onions.
Fry and crumble bacon. Add to the potato mixture along with ¼ cup bacon fat. Mix well.
Beat the eggs, and stir in the evaporated milk, melted butter, salt, and pepper.
Mix the egg mixture into the potato mixture.
Pour into a well-greased 9x13-inch cake pan—it should just barely fit.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 90 minutes.
Slice into squares, and top with sour cream or applesauce.

name: Kuih Makmur (Malaysian Peanut Cookies)
attribution: "Kuih Makmur (Malaysian Peanut Cookies)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kuih_Makmur_(Malaysian_Peanut_Cookies), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 oz fried or toasted peanuts, coarsely ground

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease or line a baking sheet.
Knead together the flour and ghee until you get a rough dough.
Divide the dough into balls about 2 inches in diameter.
Flatten one of the balls in the palm of your hand, making a little divot in the center.
Spoon about 1–2 tsp peanuts into the center of the dough. Pinch the edges of the dough together to enclose the peanuts, and gently reshape into a ball.
Place the filled cookies on the baking sheet. Bake 15–20 minutes until dried and a very light golden brown.
Carefully remove the hot cookies from the tray, and roll in powdered sugar.
Let cool and serve.

name: Kulfi (South Asian Frozen Custard)
attribution: "Kulfi (South Asian Frozen Custard)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kulfi_(South_Asian_Frozen_Custard), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ½ tsp ground green cardamom seeds

steps: Put the milk into a wide, heavy pan, and bring to boil over high heat, stirring constantly.
Lower the heat and cook the milk, stirring constantly until it has thickened and reduced to ¾ cup—this will take about 40–45 minutes. Stir the sides of the pan constantly to avoid scorching.
Stir in the sugar, nuts, and cardamom powder. Set aside to cool.
Pour the mixture evenly into kulfi moulds or small ramekins. Cover with plastic wrap or foil, and freeze for about 6 hours until set.
To serve, run a sharp knife dipped in hot water along the sides of the moulds, and unmold them onto a serving plate.

name: Kuli-kuli
attribution: "Kuli-kuli" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kuli-kuli, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ½–1 teaspoon salt or to taste

steps: Toast the peanuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring occasionally to avoid burning. Once roasted, remove the skins by rubbing them between your hands or using a cloth to gently press and peel off the skins.
Using a food processor or blender, grind the roasted peanuts to form a peanut butter, working in batches as necessary. This will take around 5–10 minutes depending on power.

Transfer peanut mixture to a large mixing bowl. Add in water, ¼ cup (60 ml) at a time, to peanut butter, kneading with your hands after each addition. This will swell up the grains in the peanut butter, making it thicker and releasing the oils. Stop adding water once the mixture starts releasing oils. Continue to knead for a further 5 minutes to release as much oil as possible.
Put the mixture into a cheesecloth, and squeeze to release the oils. Transfer the peanut mixture back to the bowl, and set aside the oils for deep-frying.
Stir in the remaining ingredients, mixing well to combine.
Mix in enough water, a tablespoon at a time, until you get a moldable dough, and knead well.

Take teaspoonfuls of the dough and roll them into small balls or form them into flat discs, depending on your preference. You can also shape them into small cylinders or oval shapes, like traditional kuli-kuli. You can experiment with different shapes.

Heat the reserved oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the kuli-kuli pieces in batches, ensuring they don’t overcrowd the pan, until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides (about 4–5 minutes). Be sure to flip them carefully to ensure even frying.
Once fried, remove the kuli-kuli from the oil and place them on a paper towel to drain excess oil. Allow them to cool completely before serving.

name: Kung Pao Chicken
attribution: "Kung Pao Chicken" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kung_Pao_Chicken, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
¼ tsp crushed red pepper flakes
1 green bell pepper, cut into ½-inch dice
1 red bell pepper, cut into ½-inch dice
1 can (5 oz) sliced bamboo shoots (optional), drained
4 green onions, cut into ½-inch pieces, including green tops

steps: Measure and prepare all ingredients before cooking.
Mix all chicken/marinade ingredients in a bowl, stir well, and allow to marinate for ½ hour.
Mix sauce ingredients in another bowl and set aside until needed. Stir out any lumps.
Heat wok or large frying pan until water drops bead up and dance on the hot surface.
Add cooking oil to wok. Wait a few seconds for oil to heat up.
Add remaining spice ingredients to wok and stir fry for 30 seconds.
Add chicken mixture to wok and stir fry for about 4 minutes (until chicken is cooked through).
Add vegetables to wok and stir fry for about 2–3 minutes.
Stir sauce and add to wok. After the sauce comes to a boil, cook for about 1 minute (until sauce thickens).
Stir to coat other ingredients with thickened sauce.
Pour onto large platter and serve immediately.

name: Kunun Aduwa (Nigerian Tiger Nut Milk)
attribution: "Kunun Aduwa (Nigerian Tiger Nut Milk)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kunun_Aduwa_(Nigerian_Tiger_Nut_Milk), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 cups dried or fresh tiger nuts (aduwa)

steps: If using dried tiger nuts, soak them in water overnight to soften, then drain and rinse them.
In a blender, combine the tiger nuts, ginger, and dates. Blend until smooth and creamy, adding water as needed to aid blending.
Strain the blended mixture using a fine sieve or cheesecloth to separate the milk from the chaff.
Chill in the refrigerator and serve cold.

name: Kunun Gyada (Groundnut and Rice Gruel)
attribution: "Kunun Gyada (Groundnut and Rice Gruel)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kunun_Gyada_(Groundnut_and_Rice_Gruel), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Soak the tamarind for 3 hours and extract the juice. Also, soak the rice and raw groundnut in separate bowls for a few hours.
Drain the groundnuts. Grind them in a blender with some water and strain the resulting groundnut milk.
Drain the rice and grind with a little water.
Boil the groundnut milk in a pot, stirring to prevent sticking and lumps. Slowly stir in the blended rice.
Stir in the tamarind juice and serve.

name: Kunun kanwa
attribution: "Kunun kanwa" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kunun_kanwa, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cup of guinea corn (or millet, sorghum, or maize) – ground into flour
1/2 teaspoon of edible potash (kanwa) or a small piece dissolved in water
1 small piece of ginger, peeled and grated
4-5 cups of water (adjust for desired consistency)
1–2 tablespoons of sugar or honey (optional, to taste)

steps: Mix the Grain flour with a little water to form a light, smooth paste. Ensure there are no lumps.
In a separate pot, dissolve the kanwa (potash) in water and bring to a light boil.
Gradually pour the boiling kanwa water into the grain paste while stirring continuously.
Keep stirring until the mixture thickens slightly into a pap-like consistency.
Allow it to simmer for 2–3 minutes. Add more water if it's too thick.
Remove from heat. Add sugar or honey if desired.
Serve hot.

name: Kunun Tamba (Finger Millet Porridge)
attribution: "Kunun Tamba (Finger Millet Porridge)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kunun_Tamba_(Finger_Millet_Porridge), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Wash the tamba and dry with a clean cloth.
Mix tamba with ginger. Grind the mixture until smooth.
Allow the ground mixture to cool down, then sieve the chaff to give a fine texture.
Boil water in a pot and add the tamba powder gradually, stirring gently to make a smooth mixture.
Add milk and sugar, then whisk until smooth and lump-free.

name: Kunun Tsamiya (Nigerian Powdered Millet and Tsamiya Drink)
attribution: "Kunun Tsamiya (Nigerian Powdered Millet and Tsamiya Drink)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kunun_Tsamiya_(Nigerian_Powdered_Millet_and_Tsamiya_Drink), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: A few pieces of dried pepper

steps: Grind together ginger, cloves, millet, and pepper until smooth, and transfer to a bowl. Mix in enough water to get a paste.
Combine the tamarind and water in a pot. Set on fire, and allow to boil for few minutes.
Slowly add the boiled water into the bowl of millet paste, stirring continuously so that it is lump-free and smooth.
Add sugar to taste and serve.

name: Kunun Zaki
attribution: "Kunun Zaki" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kunun_Zaki, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Soak the millet in water for several hours or overnight.
Wash and grind the millet with ginger and cloves into a smooth paste.
Mix the paste with water and sieve to extract the liquid.
Allow the liquid to settle for some hours, then decant the clear water on top.
Boil part of the extracted liquid while stirring continuously until it thickens slightly.
Mix the cooked portion with the remaining raw extract.
Add sugar to taste and stir well.
Allow to cool completely, then refrigerate before serving.

name: Kuwese U Logo (Nigerian Fried Cassava)
attribution: "Kuwese U Logo (Nigerian Fried Cassava)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kuwese_U_Logo_(Nigerian_Fried_Cassava), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Cut cassava into your desired size and shape, then rinse with water. Dry well.
Blend pepper and pour on sliced cassava. Toss to coat.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan.
Deep-fry the cassava in the hot oil until tender.
Remove from the oil and serve hot, sprinkled with salt.

name: Kwado (Nigerian Cassava Flour Salad)
attribution: "Kwado (Nigerian Cassava Flour Salad)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kwado_(Nigerian_Cassava_Flour_Salad), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Mash the smoked fish in a bowl.
Add the garri, ground kuli kuli, sliced onions, salt, and dry pepper.
Stir the ingredients together and serve.

name: Kwek-Kwek (Deep-Fried Quail Eggs)
attribution: "Kwek-Kwek (Deep-Fried Quail Eggs)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kwek-Kwek_(Deep-Fried_Quail_Eggs), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Pot and stove or electric fryer

steps: Gradually but vigorously whisk the water into the flour. The wet mixture should be thick but flow like a pancake batter.
Dip the eggs in the batter to coat them completely.
Heat several inches of vegetable oil in a deep pot. You're aiming for about 350°F (180°C).
Add the coated eggs to the hot oil, and deep fry until very light golden and cooked through. Remove from the oil and drain off any excess.
Serve with spicy vinegar.

name: Kyopulo (Eggplant with Peppers and Tomatoes)
attribution: "Kyopulo (Eggplant with Peppers and Tomatoes)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kyopulo_(Eggplant_with_Peppers_and_Tomatoes), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Roast the aubergines and peppers on a hot plate. Remove the skins, and cut into small pieces.
Add the tomatoes, then the crushed garlic.
Mix with a wooden spoon, then add oil, vinegar, and salt to taste. Beat together well.
Pour into a plate and top with finely chopped parsley.

name: Kyselo (Czech Sourdough Mushroom Soup)
attribution: "Kyselo (Czech Sourdough Mushroom Soup)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Kyselo_(Czech_Sourdough_Mushroom_Soup), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 100 g sourdough starter, ideally made with rye flour
15 g dried porcini mushrooms, preferably Central European
Chopped green herbs, such as parsley or scallion

steps: Boil potatoes with their skins, then peel them, chop onto small pieces and roast it in a pan (without adding grease).
Put 250 ml tepid water into a bowl. Stir in the sourdough starter. Cover with a clean cloth, and let rest at room temperature for 30 minutes to 3 hours.
Put 1000 ml water into a stockpot. Add the dried mushrooms and caraway, and boil for at least 15 minutes to make a strong broth.
Carefully add the sourdough mixture into the broth, stirring well—there is a danger that the sourdough will shrink into small dumplings.
Boil the soup, stirring, until the sourdough thickens the mixture. This should take about 10 minutes.
Sauté the chopped onion with butter in a pan. Stir it into the soup.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, and scramble them in an ungreased pan. Stir the cooked eggs into the soup.
Season the soup to taste with salt and vinegar. It should be mildly sour, flavored primarily by the mushrooms and sourdough.
Served the soup hot, garnished with the chopped herbs, with the potatoes as a side dish. Individual diners may wish to add additional vinegar and salt to taste.

name: Lafun (Nigerian Cassava Swallow)
attribution: "Lafun (Nigerian Cassava Swallow)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Lafun_(Nigerian_Cassava_Swallow), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Boil the 2 cups of water in a pot, then stir in cassava flour.
Stir in the ¼ cup hot water, and allow the mixture to steam for a few minutes.
Stir until the mixture is smooth and lump free.
Serve the lafun with your choice of soup.

name: Lahoh (Spongy Flatbread) I
attribution: "Lahoh (Spongy Flatbread) I" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Lahoh_(Spongy_Flatbread)_I, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 3 cup of wheat flour or sorghum flour
Dab of margarine or vegetable oil for greasing pan

steps: Combine semolina and ½ cup of lukewarm water in a bowl, then bring the mixture to a boil in saucepan. Remove from heat, place in a bowl, and leave to thicken.
Stir cold water into the semolina mixture.
Stir in rock salt until fully dissolved into the mixture.
Stir in the wheat flour and yeast.
Mix in another 2 cups of lukewarm water until you get a thin batter.
Cover the batter and let it rest until it is risen and bubbly.
Grease a skillet or frying pan with a little margarine, and heat over medium heat.
Ladle some batter into the pan, and let it spread out. A tiny bit of flour sprinkled in the pan helps prevent sticking.

Cook the batter until the top surface is covered with air pockets like a sponge. Flip to the other side, and cook for about 5 seconds. Remove and let cool. Repeat the cooking process with the remaining batter.

name: Lahoh (Spongy Flatbread) II
attribution: "Lahoh (Spongy Flatbread) II" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Lahoh_(Spongy_Flatbread)_II, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine all dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Add water and whisk vigorously until you get a thin batter.
Cover bowl and let sit for 1 hour.
Heat a frying pan over medium heat, and lightly grease it.
Add a ladleful of batter, and spread it out in the bottom of pan. Cook over medium heat until air bubbles form on the top of the batter.
Remove from frying pan and let cool.

name: Lamb and Okra Stew (Khoresht Bamiye)
attribution: "Lamb and Okra Stew (Khoresht Bamiye)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Lamb_and_Okra_Stew_(Khoresht_Bamiye), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 500 grams stewing lamb or beef, cut into small pieces
750 grams okra, washed with stems trimmed

steps: Fry the sliced onion in oil until slightly golden.
Add the meat and fry with the onions until the color changes.
Add 3 glasses of hot water and bring to boil. Turn heat down and let boil slowly for about 45 minutes, adding more hot water during cooking if needed.
Add okra, salt, pepper, and tomato paste to the meat. Cook for another 10–15 minutes. Take care not to overcook the okras so that they do not become slippery.
Add lime juice and adjust seasoning. Cook for another 3–4 minutes.
Serve with white rice.

name: Lamb Sausages and Grilled Potatoes
attribution: "Lamb Sausages and Grilled Potatoes" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Lamb_Sausages_and_Grilled_Potatoes, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 12 small potatoes or 10 medium sized ones weighing approximately 971g
200 g Romaine lettuce, washed and cut into smaller pieces

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C (392°F).
Rinse the potatoes, and cut into slices 0.5 cm thick using a knife, grater, or mandoline.

Put the potatoes in the cake tin, and spread them out. Add the 30 ml of olive oil to cover the entire tin and the potatoes. Sprinkle the salt all over the tin and the potatoes. Bake for 25 minutes in the preheated oven.

Heat the 15 ml olive oil and the butter in a pan over medium heat until the butter melts. Add the sausages, and cook for about 10 minutes on high heat. Turn the sausages occasionally so they fry on all sides. Remove from the heat.
Toss the lettuce and tomatoes together to make a salad.
Serve the salad with the baked potatoes and sausages.

name: Lamb Shawarma
attribution: "Lamb Shawarma" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Lamb_Shawarma, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1.5 kg leg of lamb or other tender cut

steps: Cut the lamb into large 4 cm chunks.
Combine the nutmeg, cinnamon, cardamom, garlic cloves, black pepper, cayenne pepper, lemon, and vinegar in a small mixing bowl and pour over meat.
Marinate for 2 hours or more.
Grill the onions with some garlic for few minutes.
Drain meat, pat dry, and grill until golden brown.
Serve with pita bread, tomato, fresh onion, tabbouleh, tzatziki, lettuce and chili sauce.

name: Lamington
attribution: "Lamington" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Lamington, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Cut the sponge cake into your desired shapes (commonly 5–7 cm cubes).
Prepare a flat tray with an even layer of desiccated coconut shavings
Dip the sponge cake cubes into chocolate icing.
Immediately dip the coated cake into the coconut, or sprinkle the coconut on top.
Put aside to dry and set.

name: Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
attribution: "Lancashire Corned Beef Hash" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Lancashire_Corned_Beef_Hash, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Put all the ingredients in a wok (a wok is perfect though not traditional) or another large pan.
Add water until almost covering the ingredients.
Cover and bring to boil.
Lower heat, and simmer for 30 minutes or until the potatoes soften.
If too wet, strain off some water.
Add the broken-up corned beef and stir in gently.
Bring almost to the boil.
Switch off the heat and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Heat again or serve as it is.
Put all the ingredients except the corned beef into the pressure cooker. You do not need much water—perhaps 1–2 cm.
Bring the pressure cooker up to pressure and cook for about 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, chop up the corned beef. When the other ingredients are cooked, open the pressure cooker and mix in the corned beef.
Serve.

name: Lancashire Hotpot
attribution: "Lancashire Hotpot" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Lancashire_Hotpot, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 lb (900 g) neck of lamb or mutton
1 large or 2 small white onions, diced

steps: Dice the lamb and set aside. Preheat oven to 325°F / 170°C / Gas mark 3.
Add a layer of the potatoes to the bottom of a casserole dish, and cover with a handful of the diced onion. Layer the diced lamb on top of this, sprinkling with the herbs.
Repeat these layers until the dish is full. Top with a final layer of the potatoes.
Pour boiling water into the dish until filled—if more water is needed, continue to add until topped.
Bake for at least 1 hour, though traditionally the dish was left baking all day. Mutton will require a longer cooking time.

name: Lancashire Parkin
attribution: "Lancashire Parkin" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Lancashire_Parkin, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 340 g (1 ½ cups / 12 oz) self-raising flour
