attribution: "Tuna Salad" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuna_Salad, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 can water chestnuts, drained and chopped

steps: Mix all ingredients in a bowl.
Chill before serving.
Serve on toast.

name: Tuna Salad (1940)
attribution: "Tuna Salad (1940)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuna_Salad_(1940), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ¼ cup mayonnaise (low fat can work)
½ ea. chopped green onion or ½ tsp dried chopped white or yellow onion
1 hard boiled egg, chopped (or two hard boiled egg whites and a bit of oil olive oil to make up the difference)

steps: Drain and squeeze tuna dry, discarding liquid or reserving for some other use.
Combine tuna, apple, celery, mayonnaise, lemon juice, green onion, egg, and pepper.
Refrigerate 1 hour or more.
Sprinkle with paprika and trim with lettuce, if desired.

name: Turkey & Barley Cabbage Rolls with Fresh Dill
attribution: "Turkey & Barley Cabbage Rolls with Fresh Dill" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Turkey_%26_Barley_Cabbage_Rolls_with_Fresh_Dill, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 cloves garlic, minced (or ½ tsp garlic powder)
¼ cup chopped fresh dill, loosely packed (plus extra for garnish)
1 can (796 mL) no-salt-added crushed or diced tomatoes
1 tsp maple syrup or brown sugar (optional)

steps: Simmer barley in the broth until tender (about 30–40 minutes). Drain excess liquid if needed and set aside to cool.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Core the cabbage and place it in the pot. Simmer for 5–10 minutes, removing leaves as they soften. Reserve 10–12 large leaves for rolling.
In a large bowl, make the filling by combining the cooked barley, ground turkey, onion, garlic, egg, dill, salt, and pepper.

Spread a cabbage leaf out flat on a work surface. Place 2–3 tablespoons of filling near the base of each cabbage leaf. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly to enclose the filling. Repeat with the remaining filling and cabbage leaves.

Prepare the sauce by mixing the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, canola oil, paprika, and apple cider vinegar in a bowl or large measuring cup. Add a the sugar or maple syrup if you like your sauces a bit sweeter.

Spread a few spoonfuls of the sauce on the bottom of a large baking dish or pot. Arrange the cabbage rolls over the tomatoes, seam-side down. Pour the rest of the sauce over top of the rolls Sprinkle with extra dill if desired.
For the oven method, cover with foil and bake at 175 °C (350 °F) for 1 hour. For the stovetop method, simmer gently, covered, on low heat for 1 hour.

name: Turkey and Lima Beans
attribution: "Turkey and Lima Beans" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Turkey_and_Lima_Beans, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 500 g (1 lb) minced or ground turkey
1 handful of fresh sage, chopped (or 1–2 tsp of dried sage)
1–2 tsp chile flakes or powder (or hot paprika)

steps: Soak the dried beans overnight, or at least 6 hours.

Drain the soaked beans, discarding the water. Cover the beans with water in a small pot, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Stir periodically, and start testing for tenderness after 10 minutes. Alternatively, cook in a pressure cooker at 15 PSI for 3 minutes, and set aside to depressurise.
While the beans are cooking, add olive oil to a large pan and heat. When hot, add the onion and celery, and sauté until translucent.
Add the cumin, coriander, chili, and pepper to the pan and stir in. Allow to sauté for another couple of minutes.
Add the turkey mince to the pan, and turn up the heat. Stir while browning the mince, breaking up large pieces. Ensure that all the mince is browned.
Tip the beans, with their cooking water, into the pan and stir in the salt and sage. Simmer for 15 minutes (e.g. while cooking some rice!)
Serve over steamed rice (it goes especially nicely with arborio rice)!

name: Turkey Biscuit
attribution: "Turkey Biscuit" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Turkey_Biscuit, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Sauté the onion until tender.
Combine in a small bowl the all the other ingredients except the cheese and biscuits.
Stir this mixture, then place it into a baking dish, and bake for 15 minutes at 350°F until it is quite warm throughout.
Remove the baked mixture from the oven and sprinkle the shredded cheese on it.
Add a layer of frozen biscuits on top of this. Bake for about 20–30 minutes longer.
Serve.

name: Turkish Dolma Pilav
attribution: "Turkish Dolma Pilav" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Turkish_Dolma_Pilav, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Wash the rice until the water runs clear.
Sauté pine nuts and onions over medium heat in a deep skillet with lid
Add cinnamon, mint, salt, sugar and black pepper
Add the rice and stir constantly until the rice turns translucent
Add water, enough to cover the rice and cook on low heat.
When the water is absorbed, check the rice. Add more water or spices if needed.
Quickly add currants; they should soften in the steam but can be soaked in hot water if preferred.
If needed, use paper towel and a pan with a closed lid to steam the rice until it is finished cooking.

name: Turmeric Chicken and Asparagus Stir-Fry
attribution: "Turmeric Chicken and Asparagus Stir-Fry" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Turmeric_Chicken_and_Asparagus_Stir-Fry, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thigh, cut in 1 inch (2–3 cm) pieces

steps: 1–3 tbsp coconut or neutral oil
1 lb asparagus, trimmed and thinly sliced on the bias
Kosher salt
1 tsp rice vinegar
1 ea. lime, juiced
Seasoned wok or cast-iron skillet
Combine the water, honey, pepper, and salt to make the sauce. Set aside.
Combine the flour, turmeric, and salt together. Sprinkle over the chicken, and immediately toss to coat the chicken well.
Heat the oil in your pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, and cook, tossing as needed, until golden brown all over. If it starts darkening too quickly, lower the heat.
Add the asparagus to the pan, and season with a pinch of salt. Cook for 1–2 minutes, or until tender but still crisp. Note that the asparagus will continue cooking.
Stir in the prepared sauce, and simmer everything until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened to your taste (about 2–3 minutes).
Remove from the heat, and stir in the rice vinegar and lime juice. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt, pepper, vinegar, and lime to taste.

name: Tuscan Bean Soup
attribution: "Tuscan Bean Soup" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuscan_Bean_Soup, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cup spelt or wheat berries (available at gourmet-food shops)
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
½ pound sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
1 pound kale, preferably Tuscan, coarse stems removed, cut into thick ribbons
1 large rib celery, trimmed and diced
5 cups homemade chicken stock, or canned low-sodium stock, plus more if needed
1 cup peeled, seeded, and diced tomatoes, or drained canned diced tomatoes
Sea salt and freshly ground pepper
½ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese

steps: Soak beans and spelt overnight in separate bowls of cold water.
Drain and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add sausage.
Cook stirring occasionally, until meat begins to separate and brown (3–5 minutes).
Stir in kale, onion, carrot, celery, and garlic.
Cook until softened (about 10 minutes).
Add beans, spelt, chicken stock, and tomatoes.
Bring to boil.
Stir in rosemary and sage.
Reduce heat.
Simmer mixture for 60–70 minutes, until beans are tender; if soup is too thick, add chicken stock.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Ladle soup into bowls.
Drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle on cheese.
Serve immediately.

name: Tuscan Mushroom Risotto
attribution: "Tuscan Mushroom Risotto" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuscan_Mushroom_Risotto, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 5 cups chicken broth or vegetable broth
1 cup choice of Parmesan, Romano cheese, or Asiago cheese
Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

steps: Keep broth heated in a medium-size saucepan.
On medium heat in a large pan combine butter, garlic or garlic oil, shallots, mushrooms, and rice.
Heat for about 2 minutes, stirring well.
Add white wine and let simmer on low for 2 minutes.
With lid off, add chicken or vegetable broth, add cream, and let simmer on low until liquid is absorbed, approximately 25 minutes, stirring regularly.
Add cheese of choice and salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with parsley and grated choice.

name: Tuscan Roast Potatoes
attribution: "Tuscan Roast Potatoes" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuscan_Roast_Potatoes, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 pound (450 g) each Russet potatoes and redskin potatoes, cut into 2-inch (5 cm) cubes
1 ½ tsp each dried parsley, rosemary, thyme, basil and oregano

steps: Heat a large pot of water to a boil. Add potatoes and cook for 10 minutes. Shock in a bowl of ice water.
Drain and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Combine remaining ingredients. Add potatoes and toss to coat.
Spread out in one even layer on your largest baking pan. Roast at 450°F (230°C) for 20 minutes, stirring halfway.
Serve warm.

name: Tuscan Soup (Meatless)
attribution: "Tuscan Soup (Meatless)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuscan_Soup_(Meatless), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 can (15–16 ounces) kidney beans or great northern beans, rinsed and drained
⅔ cup uncooked small spiral pasta
3 cups thinly-sliced fresh escarole or spinach

steps: In a 2-quart saucepan, sauté onion and carrot in oil until onion is tender.
Add broth, water, salt and pepper; bring to a boil.
Stir in beans and pasta; return to a boil.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 15 minutes or until pasta and vegetables are tender, stirring occasionally.
Add escarole or spinach and heat through.

name: Tuwo Alabo (Nigerian Cassava Swallow)
attribution: "Tuwo Alabo (Nigerian Cassava Swallow)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuwo_Alabo_(Nigerian_Cassava_Swallow), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Sift the cassava flour to remove debris.
Boil the water in a pot, and gradually stir in the flour until it forms a smooth mixture.
Use the wooden spatula to mix and mash the dough until smooth and thick.
Cover the pot and allow the mixture to steam on low heat for 3–5 minutes.
Stir again until well-cooked and smooth.

name: Tuwo Alkama (Wheat Swallow)
attribution: "Tuwo Alkama (Wheat Swallow)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuwo_Alkama_(Wheat_Swallow), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Sift the flour to remove any debris.
Bring a saucepan of water to a boil. Gradually and continuously stir in the flour until it forms a thick mixture.
Cook for 5 minutes, then serve.

name: Tuwo Dawa
attribution: "Tuwo Dawa" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuwo_Dawa, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Boil water in a pot until it reaches a rolling boil.
Gradually add millet flour while stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat and continue stirring until the mixture thickens.
Add small amounts of water if needed to adjust consistency.
Continue stirring until smooth and stretchy.
Cover and allow to cook on low heat for a few minutes.
Stir again and shape into a smooth mound.
Serve hot with soup.

name: Tuwo Masara (Nigerian Corn Fufu)
attribution: "Tuwo Masara (Nigerian Corn Fufu)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuwo_Masara_(Nigerian_Corn_Fufu), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Boil water in a pot; In a medium-sized pot, bring about 4 cups of water to a boil. Reserve the remaining 1 cup of water for adjustments.
Add corn flour gradually, stirring until it forms a thick and stretchy mix.
Add a little water to the mixture until it reaches your desired consistency. Cover the pot and cook for a few minutes.
Mould tuwo masara into balls and serve.

name: Tuwo Shinkafa (Nigerian Mashed Rice)
attribution: "Tuwo Shinkafa (Nigerian Mashed Rice)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuwo_Shinkafa_(Nigerian_Mashed_Rice), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 500 g (2 milk tin cups) short-grain non-parboiled rice
Water (about twice the volume of the rice)

steps: Wash the rice thoroughly, then drain.
Add water to pot and bring to a boil.
Add the rinsed rice to the pot of boiling water.
Simmer the rice until the water is absorbed and the rice is soft and sticky. If the rice hasn't softened when all the water is gone, add additional water as needed.
Use the spatula to thoroughly mash the soft rice until it forms a soft dough.
Mold into desired container and allow to take shape of the container or wrap inside nylon
Serve hot with your preferred soup.

name: Tuwon Dawa (Nigerian Sorghum Swallow)
attribution: "Tuwon Dawa (Nigerian Sorghum Swallow)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tuwon_Dawa_(Nigerian_Sorghum_Swallow), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 cups whole guinea corn (sorghum) or 1½ cups sorghum flour
Wooden spoon or turmi (local wooden spatula)

steps: If using whole sorghum, wash the grains thoroughly and spread them out to dry completely, covering them to keep out dust and debris. Grind or pound the dried grains into a fine powder. Sieve to remove any chaff.
In a pot, bring 3–4 cups of water to a boil.
Mix some of the sorghum flour with a small amount of water to form a smooth, semi-thick batter.
Gradually stir the batter into the boiling water, mixing continuously to avoid lumps.
Add potash, and stir well. Allow to cook on medium heat, stirring regularly, until the mixture thickens.
For a firmer tuwo, add more sorghum flour directly and stir vigorously until it reaches the desired consistency.
Once cooked, mold and serve hot with soup.

name: Twice-Baked Potatoes I
attribution: "Twice-Baked Potatoes I" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Twice-Baked_Potatoes_I, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Vegetable oil to rub on potato skins
A pinch of ground black pepper

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Rub potato skins with vegetable oil to ensure crispness.
Bake potatoes for 1 hour until done.
Carefully remove potatoes from oven and cool for 10 minutes.
Cut potatoes in half lengthwise and scoop out pulp with a small spoon, leaving only a potato shell.
Mash potato pulp with a fork until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients until well combined. It is better if the mixture is a bit stiff, rather than entirely wet. Adjust the amount of milk accordingly.
Spoon (or pipe) the mixture into the empty potato shells.
If desired, top the potatoes with bell pepper, onions, and/or bacon.
Increase oven setting to broil.
Broil potatoes 10 or 15 minutes until spotty brown and crisp.

name: Twice-Baked Potatoes II
attribution: "Twice-Baked Potatoes II" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Twice-Baked_Potatoes_II, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Pierce potato skins with a fork and wrap in foil.
Bake potatoes for 1 hour or until soft.
Reduce oven temperature to 350°F.
Carefully remove potatoes from oven and cool for 10 minutes.
Cut potatoes at top ⅓ lengthwise and remove tops.
Scoop out pulp with a small spoon, to about ¼ inch from skin.
Mash potato pulp with a fork until smooth.
Add butter, sour cream, ½ cup shredded cheese, heavy cream, milk, salt, and pepper, mash until well combined and smooth.
Stir in bacon and onion.
Spoon or pipe the mixture into the empty potato shells.
Top with the rest of the cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes, or until cheese is melted.

name: Tzatziki
attribution: "Tzatziki" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Tzatziki, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon dill (sub. ¼ tablespoon of tarragon if no dill is available)

steps: Drain yogurt in a sieve or a cheesecloth for about 3 hours prior to using it.
Drain the cucumber and salt it to further remove moisture.
Combine yogurt, garlic, olive oil, and lemon juice in a bowl and cover and refrigerate for 1 hour or more.
After refrigerating, add dill and cucumber into bowl and mix with a whisk until smooth.
Add pepper and salt to taste.

name: Ugba na Ukpaka
attribution: "Ugba na Ukpaka" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Ugba_na_Ukpaka, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Small pot (if fish or stockfish is used)

steps: If using dried fish or stockfish, soak in hot water and cook until soft. Clean and set aside.
Slice the onions and utazi leaves into thin pieces.
Place ugba (oil bean seeds) in a clean bowl.
Add palm oil and mix thoroughly until the ugba is evenly coated.
Add ground crayfish, pepper, and salt, and stir well.
Add the cooked fish or stockfish (if using) and mix gently.
Add sliced onions and utazi leaves and combine evenly.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Allow to sit for a few minutes for flavors to blend.
Serve as a side dish with yam, garri (eba), or other staples.

name: Ukazi Soup
attribution: "Ukazi Soup" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Ukazi_Soup, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 ea. "cameroon peppers" or yellow habanero chiles, chopped

steps: Boil the meat and fish in water with stock cubes until the meat is tender.
Stir in the palm oil and chiles. Cook until yellow.
Reduce the heat and stir in the achara and crayfish.
Season to taste with stock cubes and salt, then cook for 5 more minutes.
Stir in the okazi leaf, and cook for 3 minutes.

name: Ukpo Oka (Nigerian Corn Pudding)
attribution: "Ukpo Oka (Nigerian Corn Pudding)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Ukpo_Oka_(Nigerian_Corn_Pudding), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Blend together the corn, pepper, onion, and crayfish with a small amount of water.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl, and stir in salt and palm oil to taste.
Pour the mixture into a mold. Place in boiling water, and steam for 45 minutes.

name: Ukrainian Borscht
attribution: "Ukrainian Borscht" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Ukrainian_Borscht, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ½ cup dried beans, soaked in water overnight
1 large or 2 medium beets, peeled and julienne
Herbs and spices: salt, bay leaf, black pepper, red pepper flakes, thyme
3 ounces salted pork fat or bacon

steps: Drain the soaked beans and put aside.
Place the meat in a large pot, and add 3 cups of cold water.
Bring to a boil slowly and remove scum.
Add half of the onion and 2 carrots.
Reduce to a simmer, partially cover the pot, and cook for about 1 hour.
When done, add the beets and beans, and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the beans are tender.
In the vegetable oil, sweat half of the onion, carrots, and green pepper over low heat until the onions are yellow.
Scrape into the pot, and simmer for a few minutes. Scrape in tomatoes, potatoes, and spices, and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Add the cabbage and simmer until it has the consistency you like.
In the meantime, chop the garlic, dill, and pork fat (or bacon) in the food processor, whisking in the yoghurt at the end.
When the cabbage is the way you like it, add tomato paste and the garlic-dill-fat mixture.
Return the pot to a simmer, then cover the pot, turn the heat off, and let the flavors mingle for at least 30 minutes.
When ready to serve, ladle into bowls and top the soup with a dollop of sour cream on top.

name: Ukrainian Cabbage Soup (Kapusniak)
attribution: "Ukrainian Cabbage Soup (Kapusniak)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Ukrainian_Cabbage_Soup_(Kapusniak), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2–5 cloves of garlic, peeled and minced
1–2 potatoes, peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces
4–6 carrots, peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces
4–5 sticks of celery, sliced into bite-sized pieces

steps: In a large cooking pot heat about 3–4 tablespoons of olive oil. Add the onions and garlic, along with more olive oil if necessary. Let the onions and garlic cook over medium or low heat for 8–10 minutes.
Add the chicken broth, and bring to a boil.

Add the potatoes, carrots, celery, and spices; bring to a boil, and simmer over medium heat until vegetables are almost tender enough to eat. If the soup becomes too thick, add some more chicken broth, but it should be a hearty soup with plenty of vegetables.
Season with salt, pepper, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, seasoning salt, garlic salt, and or celery salt as desired.
Add the can of tomatoes and the shredded cabbage. Again, let the soup simmer over medium heat; continue tasting to see whether your imagination has worked magic.
Lastly, add the chopped fresh dill.
When it’s done, serve garnished with sour cream.

name: Upeseru (Indian Lentils with Greens)
attribution: "Upeseru (Indian Lentils with Greens)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Upeseru_(Indian_Lentils_with_Greens), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1½ cups dhal or other lentils, cooked but not drained
5 handfuls of a leafy green such as spinach, chopped
1–6 green chillies, split lengthwise, according to taste
½ teaspoon fresh tamarind per chilli used

steps: Fry the mustard seed, curry leaves, onion and green chillies in oil until the onions are partly browned.
Meanwhile, set the lentils on the stove. Add the chopped spinach and boil until the spinach is tender.
Drain and set the water aside separately for the next part.
Stir in the spice mixture and salt to taste, keeping on the heat until the flavours have blended.
Dry-roast the chillies and tamarind slightly, if desired.
Grind all dry ingredients together with a little water to make a chutney.
Bring the spinach broth to a boil and let simmer for 2 minutes.
When serving, mix in a spoonful of the chutney and squeeze in lemon juice.
Eat with mudde (ragi balls).

name: Uturu Oka
attribution: "Uturu Oka" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Uturu_Oka, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Wash the maize thoroughly and soak it in clean water for 1–2 days to allow fermentation.
Change the water once daily if needed to avoid spoilage.
After fermentation, drain the water and grind or blend the maize into a smooth paste.
Pour the mixture into a pot and add fresh water while stirring to prevent lumps.
Place the pot on heat and stir continuously as it begins to thicken.
Cook until it forms a smooth, thick porridge consistency.
Add sugar, milk, or salt depending on preference.
Stir well and allow to simmer for a few minutes.
Remove from heat and serve warm.

name: Valencian-Inspired Paella
attribution: "Valencian-Inspired Paella" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Valencian-Inspired_Paella, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 500 g (1 pound) boneless, skinless chicken, diced
1 large whole rabbit (or additional pound of chicken breast as a substitute)
3 large red bell peppers, one cut into strips and the remaining diced
500 g (1 pound) diced or grated tomatoes
500 g (1 pound) canned cannellini beans in water, thoroughly rinsed
8–10 threads of saffron and/or 1.5 teaspoons yellow food coloring
3 cups short-grain white rice (also called Valencian rice or pearl rice)
Clean, white towel large enough to cover the paellera
A stove large enough to accommodate the size of the paellera
A gas burner designed specifically for paelleras
A low, forged steel tripod to support the paellera over a wood or charcoal fire
Cinder blocks or heat-resistant bricks to support the paellera over a wood or charcoal fire

steps: Defrost the duck if necessary.
Remove the organs and orange sauce packet and set aside.
Cut off the tail, trim off the neck skin and set aside.
Quarter the duck.
Place the quartered duck, spine, neck skin and tail in the pot along with the frozen rabbit and the onion and green bell pepper.
Fill the pot nearly to the top with water and heat to a moderate boil. Allow the contents to boil for about an hour.
Remove the rabbit and quartered duck but leave the neck, tail and spine in the water. Then allow it to cool. All the meat should be cooked.
Remove the skin from the duck meat and place the skin back in the pot.
Remove the meat from the rabbit and duck and set aside.
Put the duck bones, duck skin and rabbit bones back in the boiling water.
Boil until the water is reduced to half of its original volume.
Discard the bones and skin and strain the broth.
Add the saffron and/or food coloring and simmer for an additional 2–3 minutes until the broth turns orange/yellow.
Cut off the stems and thoroughly rinse the artichokes.
Boil both the stems and the artichoke for about 20 minutes.
Remove from the pot and run under cold water until cool.
Cut the leaves from the artichoke hearts and scoop out the spiny threads. You will use the hearts and stems in the paella. Save the leaves for another day.
Pour olive oil in a paellera over high heat and wait for the oil to shimmer.
Sear the pepper strips and remove from the pan.
Add the chicken breast and a tablespoon of salt. Cook the chicken about half way.
Add the duck and rabbit. Sauté the meat until golden brown.
Add diced peppers and sauté for 1 minute.
Create a space in the center of the pan and add the garlic. Sauté until brown (be careful, as garlic burns easily).
In the same space, add the tomatoes and allow to cook for about a minute. Then mix thoroughly.
Add the paprika and mix thoroughly.
Add the rice and stir until the rice is coated with the mixture.
Pat the mixture down so it's level and add the broth so that it's almost to the top of the paellera.
Add the rosemary branches, artichoke hearts and stems.
Reduce the heat to low and allow the mixture to simmer for 10 minutes.
Taste the broth. Add more salt if needed and gently mix to prevent broth from spilling.
Remove the rosemary branches and continue cooking. At this point it's important NOT to stir the paella to allow toasted rice to develop at the bottom of the pan.
Taste the rice in various places about once every four to five minutes. You'll know it's done when it's soft but not pasty.
Replace the bell pepper strips and arrange them in a circular pattern.
Remove the paella from the heat and place a white dish towel over the pan.
Wait 5–10 minutes to allow the rice to absorb the remaining liquid.
Serve hot. You should notice toasted (but not burned) rice at the bottom of the pan.

name: Valentine's Day Chocolate Cake
attribution: "Valentine's Day Chocolate Cake" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Valentine's_Day_Chocolate_Cake, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ¼ cup (60 g) light corn syrup

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Grease and flour 12-cup Bundt pan, set aside.
Combine flour, baking powder, soda, and salt in mixing bowl, set aside.
In separate bowl, microwave 1 bag chocolate hearts until melted (about 1½ minutes), stopping to stir occasionally; set aside.
In large bowl, beat shortening, sugar, and orange zest until fluffy; add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
In another bowl, combine milk and sour cream.
With electric mixer on low, alternately add flour and milk mixtures into shortening mixture, beating until smooth.
Stir 1 cup cake batter into cooled melted chocolate; set aside.
Spoon half of plain batter into bottom of prepared pan.
Cover with all the chocolate batter
Top with remaining plain batter.
Bake for 55–60 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Remove from oven to wire rack, cook completely.
From 1 bag chocolate hearts, set aside 8.
In microwave-safe bowl, combine remaining chocolate hearts, corn syrup, and heavy cream.
Heat in microwave oven 1–2 minutes, stirring frequently until smooth.
Cool slightly.
Remove cake from pan to wire rack set over sheet pan covered with waxed paper.
Spoon glaze over cake, allowing excess to drip.
Decorate with reserved chocolate hearts.

name: Vanilla Coconut Caramel
attribution: "Vanilla Coconut Caramel" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vanilla_Coconut_Caramel, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cup light corn syrup or cane syrup

steps: Boil sugar, corn syrup, margarine, and coconut milk to firm-ball stage (245°F).
Remove from heat and add vanilla.
Serve warm.

name: Vanilla Crisps
attribution: "Vanilla Crisps" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vanilla_Crisps, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Cream butter, shortening and sugar together.
Add salt and vanilla.
One at a time, beat eggs into mixture.
Stir flour into mixture to make dough.
Roll dough into small balls and press into circular shapes on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake for 8–10 minutes.
Remove immediately from pan and allow to cool.

name: Vanilla Ice Cream (Egg-Free)
attribution: "Vanilla Ice Cream (Egg-Free)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vanilla_Ice_Cream_(Egg-Free), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine all ingredients in an ice cream machine.
Run the machine according to the manufacturer's directions.
Transfer ice cream to a container, and freeze for a few hours until solid.

name: Vanillekipferl (Almond Crescent Cookies)
attribution: "Vanillekipferl (Almond Crescent Cookies)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vanillekipferl_(Almond_Crescent_Cookies), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Sift the flour into a bowl.
Cut the cold butter into slices and mix it with the flour.
Add icing sugar, salt, vanilla sugar, ground almonds, and egg to the mixture.
Rinse hands in cold water, and knead the dough on a pastry board. Let the dough rest for half an hour.
Grease a baking tray, or alternatively use a sheet of baking paper to prevent the kipferl from sticking.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F/Gas 4 ).
Form the dough to a cylinder with a diameter of approximately 5 cm, and cut off 0.5 cm thick slices. Roll them between your flat palms to form a sausage shape that is slightly tapered.
Lay them in crescent shape on the baking tray, and bake them for 8–10 minutes until they are a light golden brown.
Immediately after baking, dip the Kipferl into a mixture of icing sugar and vanilla sugar. Try some—they are delicious while still warm!
Leave the rest out overnight, and then store them in an airtight tin.

name: Vegan Gingerbread Cake
attribution: "Vegan Gingerbread Cake" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vegan_Gingerbread_Cake, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cup (240 ml) all-purpose flour or a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend
⅓ cup (240 ml) granulated cane sugar
2 tablespoon (15 ml) coconut oil, melted and cooled

steps: Combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, salt, and sugar in the large bowl.
Whisk together the almond milk, coconut oil, applesauce, molasses, and vanilla in the medium bowl.
Mix the wet with the dry ingredients successively.
Grease the baking pan and fill it with the batter.
Bake for 12 minutes at 190 °C (375 °F) or until it tests clean when a skewer is inserted into the center.
Cool and unmold the cake.

name: Vegemite Sandwich
attribution: "Vegemite Sandwich" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vegemite_Sandwich, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Toast the bread slices.
Spread butter thickly and evenly on bread.
Spread Vegemite a little less thickly, and evenly on bread.
Add cheese and onion.

name: Vegetable Salad
attribution: "Vegetable Salad" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vegetable_Salad, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 300 g bean sprouts, washed in hot water
6 sheets lettuce, washed and cut into 6 pieces
6 cucumber, peeled and sliced 1 cm thick
4 hard-boiled eggs, each cut into 4 pieces

steps: Mix all the vegetables ingredients on a bowl, and allow to rest for until 5 minutes.
Mix all the sauce ingredients with spoon.
Place the sauce, reserving 2 tbsp, into the vegetable mixture, and then mix again.
Top with egg quarters, then top eggs with reserved sauce.

name: Vegetable Soup
attribution: "Vegetable Soup" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vegetable_Soup, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 slice of bread, toasted and buttered

steps: Boil the onion, turnip, potatoes, carrot, and celery in the water until the vegetables are cooked.
Insert the bread into a bowl. Pour the soup over it.

name: Vegetable Stew and Dumplings
attribution: "Vegetable Stew and Dumplings" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vegetable_Stew_and_Dumplings, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Margarine or olive oil (or a mixture of both)
1 large green bell pepper, roughly chopped
1 large red bell pepper, roughly chopped
1 dessert spoon (2.5 teaspoons) yeast extract spread (Marmite)
1 tin (260 g) butter beans or chickpeas (or a mix of both)
½ cup (200 g) frozen or fresh garden peas

steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into roughly 4 cm (1½-inch) chunks.
On low heat, heat the margarine in a large saucepan. Add the potatoes, carrots, onions, celery, and bell peppers. Stir, making sure all vegetables get a good coating of the oil.
Gently fry/sweat the vegetables for 3 minutes and season well, then add the flour and continue to stir and coat all the vegetables.
Stir in the tin of chopped tomatoes and the tomato paste, then add enough water to cover all the ingredients in the pan.
Simmer gently for a further 3 minutes, occasionally stirring.
Stir in the stock/bouillon, yeast extract, and garlic.

Place a lid on (with a slight gap to allow some of the steam to escape), and gently simmer on a low heat for 35–50 minutes. Stir occasionally to prevent the ingredients from sticking to the bottom of the pan and burning.
Make the dumpling mixture: Sift the self-raising flour, baking powder, and baking soda into a large bowl. Cut the margarine into the flour, and add a pinch of salt and fresh ground pepper.
Add a very small quantity of cold water and pinch-mix with your fingers (you can always add more later), just enough to make a strong, sticky dough.

Test the main stew to see if it's ready for adding the dumpling dough. Take a carrot from the pan and if it feels semi-cooked, but still firm, then it is the perfect time to add the butter beans and peas.
Taste, then adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if necessary.
Distribute walnut-sized lumps of dough, evenly spaced, on top of the simmering stew.
Replace the lid and cook for a further 20–25 minutes, at which time you should have large, light and fluffy dumplings.
Serve the stew and dumplings piping hot straight from the pan with fresh crusty bread and prepared yellow mustard on the side.

name: Vegetarian Rassolnik
attribution: "Vegetarian Rassolnik" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vegetarian_Rassolnik, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Bring water to boil. Add the sliced potatoes, cucumbers, carrots, and onions.
When the vegetables are cooked, add the cooked rice, bay leaf, and oil.
Bring to a boil.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve garnished with chopped herbs.

name: Vegetarian Soft Tacos
attribution: "Vegetarian Soft Tacos" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vegetarian_Soft_Tacos, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 pound ground beef substitute (e.g. MorningStar Farms Grillers Recipe Crumbles)

steps: In a frying pan brown onions on medium-low heat.
Add garlic, chilli powder, paprika, salt, and red pepper. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Add beef substitute and water. Cook for 10–15 minutes until most of the water is gone.
Meanwhile chop and shred the toppings as needed. Put toppings in bowls on table.
Start to warm refried beans in a small pot.
Heat another frying pan on medium-low heat.
Put vegetarian taco meat and refried beans in bowls and place on table.
Put floured tortilla in pan and lightly brown both sides. As tortillas are ready allow guests to select their own toppings.

name: Veggie Pizza
attribution: "Veggie Pizza" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Veggie_Pizza, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 pre-made pizza crust, rolled to 30 cm (12 inches) across
½ ea. green bell pepper, de-seeded and thinly sliced
½ cup thinly sliced baby bella mushrooms
4½ tbsp pitted and sliced black olives

steps: Preheat oven to 240° C (450° F / Gas 9).
Brush the dough surface with olive oil.
Ladle the sauce over the dough, spreading it evenly.
Distribute the cheeses evenly over the crust.

Lay the toppings evenly over the cheese. If needed, press toppings down with a utensil to provide clearance from the oven ceiling. If desired, top the vegetables with extra cheese and sauce to hold vegetables down.
Bake pizza in oven until crust edges are deep dark brown (roughly 15 minutes for pre-made crust, much longer for freshly made dough).
Take pizza out of oven and let cool.

name: Veggie Salad
attribution: "Veggie Salad" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Veggie_Salad, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Cut the green pepper into long thin strips.
Toss vegetables together in a large bowl.
Using a mortar, grind the spices together, and sprinkle over salad.
Sprinkle walnut chunks over salad.
Serve.

name: Velouté Sauce
attribution: "Velouté Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Velout%C3%A9_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Make a white roux: melt the butter in a sauce pan over low heat until the foam subsides. Whisk in the flour and cook slowly, while stirring until the mixture froths up for about 2 minutes. The flour should lose its raw smell but not its color.
Remove from the heat. When the roux has stopped bubbling, slowly incorporate the stock, whisking quickly but smoothly to create a smooth mixture.
Add the seasonings and cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently. Simmer the sauce until it lightly coats the back of a spoon.
Taste and adjust seasonings.

name: Venetian Soup
attribution: "Venetian Soup" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Venetian_Soup, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour, and cook to make a white roux.
Gradually mix in the warm stock, then the grated cheese to form a paste.
Remove from the heat, and mix in the egg yolks. Shape the mixture into little quenelles.
Boil the quenelles in a little broth, then drain them.
Serve the quenelles in additional broth.

name: Venison Bolognese Sauce
attribution: "Venison Bolognese Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Venison_Bolognese_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive, corn or sunflower oil (according to taste)
500 g (1.1 lb) minced/ground) stewing venison (minced lean leftovers from trimming are ideal)
500 ml dry hard cider, red or white wine, or beef stock (how much you will need depends on how fast it boils away)
300 g (¾ lb) penne, spaghetti or whatever other pasta you prefer

steps: Sauté the onions, mushrooms, and garlic in the oil until well softened.
Add the venison and stir well until it has all (more or less) changed colour.
Add sufficient dry cider to cover, but not too deeply.
Add the stock cube (only if you are using wine or cider), bay leaves, grated carrot, and tomato purée, and stir well.

Simmer very gently for at least 3 hours, stirring occasionally and replenishing the liquid (with more cider/wine/stock or just water) if it gets too dry. The ideal is to have the sauce with little separate liquid when it is served, but not dry enough to scorch. It may be simmered on top of the stove, or in a very low oven, or in a slow cooker. The sauce is edible after about 40 minutes but is infinitely better flavoured and textured after 3 or 4 hours. In a slow cooker it can be cooked for 8 hours. The flavour is even better if it is cooked, allowed to cool overnight, and reheated for 30 or 40 minutes—but, this is a council of perfection and not really necessary.
About 30–40 minutes before serving remove the bay leaves, add the herbes de Provence, and adjust the salt (i.e. taste it and add more salt if you think it needs it).
Just before serving, add freshly-ground black pepper.
Serve over al dente pasta sprinkled with grated Parmesan cheese.

name: Venison Italian Style
attribution: "Venison Italian Style" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Venison_Italian_Style, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Slice loin across grain into ¼-inch or thinner slices, or pound flat between two pieces of waxed paper.
Combine with 1 cup of milk in shallow dish.
Cover dish in refrigerator for up to 3 hours, then discard milk.
Add remaining milk and temper outside refrigerator for 1 hour.
Discard milk, then pat slices dry.
Mix flour, salt and pepper, then thoroughly coat venison slices.
In large skillet, melt butter over medium heat, then brown venison on both sides.
Add wine and simmer two minutes more.
Transfer venison slices to heated platter with slotted spoon.
Add lemon juice, capers, and parsley to skillet, and cook on medium two minutes, constantly scraping bottom and sides of skillet.
Serve venison slices with sauce over it.

name: Very Simple Cookies
attribution: "Very Simple Cookies" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Very_Simple_Cookies, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 sticks (1 cup, 8 ounces, or 225 g) butter, melted

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Combine the sugar and melted butter.
Mix in the flour until you have a thick dough.
Mix in the chocolate chips and oats, if using.
Shape the dough into your desired cookie shapes. Transfer to a greased or parchment-lined baking sheet.
Put the cookies in the oven. Bake until the cookies are a golden colour and are hard (probably 8–12 minutes, depending on size), and then take them out.

name: Vichyssoise (Chilled Potato Leek Soup)
attribution: "Vichyssoise (Chilled Potato Leek Soup)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vichyssoise_(Chilled_Potato_Leek_Soup), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 4 large diced leeks (white and yellow parts only)
1 bunch diced shallots (white bases only) or green onions
1½ tbsp chicken bouillon or add homemade stock

steps: Peel potatoes and remove all brown and discolored areas.
Boil potatoes for 20 minutes or until the interiors are soft when stuck with a knife. Do not overcook potatoes.
Drain potatoes, retain liquid, let the potatoes cool, then mash with fork.
In a braiser over low heat, sauté leek and shallot bottoms in the butter until translucent, or about 10 minutes.
Add chicken base, white pepper, white wine, heavy cream, and milk; simmer until soup starts to bubble.
Add mashed potatoes and whisk vigorously; if the soup is too thick add some of the potato water.
Chill the soup.
Just before serving, put the soup in a blender, and blend on low speed for 20 seconds. Garnish with shallot tops

name: Vietnamese Caramel Sauce (Nước Maøu)
attribution: "Vietnamese Caramel Sauce (Nước Maøu)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vietnamese_Caramel_Sauce_(N%C6%B0%E1%BB%9Bc_Ma%C3%B8u), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ¼ cup water or fish sauce

steps: Combine sugar and the ¼ cup water/fish sauce in a small saucepan over low heat.
Swirl the pan frequently to avoid burning. When the sugar turns light brown, remove from the heat.
Stir in the 1 cup of water/fish sauce. Guard against splattering.
Let cool a little and return the sauce to the stove. Cook on low heat until all the sugar has dissolved.
Let the sauce cool and store in a jar in the refrigerator for future use.

name: Vietnamese Fish Dipping Sauce (Nước mắm pha)
attribution: "Vietnamese Fish Dipping Sauce (Nước mắm pha)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Vietnamese_Fish_Dipping_Sauce_(N%C6%B0%E1%BB%9Bc_m%E1%BA%AFm_pha), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ¼ cups nước mắm (concentrated fish sauce)
1 tsp minced garlic or about 2 cloves pressed through a garlic press
½ tsp sambal oelek (a type of hot chile sauce)

steps: Mix all ingredients together.
If desired, bring to a boil that cannot be stirred down.
Cover and refrigerate.

name: Violet Lemonade
attribution: "Violet Lemonade" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Violet_Lemonade, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 cups wild violets, stems and leaves removed

steps: Steep the violets in hot water for at least 10 minutes or until it turns a dark blue hue. Strain and reserve the liquid.
Stir the sugar into the violet tea until dissolved to create a simple syrup.
Combine the cold water with the lemon juice.
Serve the lemon mixture over ice, and garnish with extra flowers. When ready to drink, pour the syrup into the lemon water and watch it turn from a dark blue to a bright pink color.

name: Waakye (Ghanian Rice and Beans)
attribution: "Waakye (Ghanian Rice and Beans)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Waakye_(Ghanian_Rice_and_Beans), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 3–4 leaves of Guinea corn leaves, washed
1 milk tin (14 fl oz) beans, washed
2 milk tins (28 fl oz) brown or white rice, washed

steps: Half-fill a saucepan with water, and place over the fire. Add the Guinea corn leaves.
Bring to a boil, and add the beans.
Simmer for 40-45 minutes until the beans split in two when touched.
Add the rice and salt, and simmer until the beans and rice are very soft. Add additional water as necessary during the cooking.
Remove from the heat. Serve with shito and fried tomato stew, accompanied by wele, tilapia, boiled eggs, and salad.

name: Wacky Cake
attribution: "Wacky Cake" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wacky_Cake, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine flour, sugar, cocoa, and baking soda in a large bowl.
Add water, oil, vinegar and vanilla. Blend thoroughly.
Pour into a greased square cake pan.
Bake at 180°C or 350°F for 35–40 minutes.
Cool completely.

name: Wakeup Sausage Casserole
attribution: "Wakeup Sausage Casserole" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wakeup_Sausage_Casserole, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 24 ounces evaporated milk (or substitute 3 cups of milk)
1 pound hot bulk pork sausage, cooked, drained, and crumbled
8 cups (8–10 slices) ½-inch cubed French or Italian bread (ideally a day old or a little stale)

steps: Preheat oven to .
Grease a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Place bread cubes in the pan evenly.
Combine eggs, garlic powder, green onion tops, evaporated milk, onion powder, and mustard.
Pour into baking dish.
Crumble sausage over the mixture evenly.
Add cheese and peppers, if desired, over the top.
If preparing ahead, cover and refrigerate.
Bake until set, about 45 minutes.
Serve warm.

name: Waldorf Salad
attribution: "Waldorf Salad" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Waldorf_Salad, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 80 g (⅓ cup or 3 oz) chopped walnuts
80 g (⅓ cup or 3 oz) chopped celery

steps: Slice the apples into wedges, and place in a bowl.
Pour lemon juice on the apple wedges, and ensure a light coating to prevent browning.
Plump the raisins by placing them in warm water for 5 minutes, then drain well.
Mix celery, raisins, and walnuts into the bowl of apple wedges.
Mix the mayonnaise and sugar together, then pour into the apple mixture, ensuring a light coating on all items.
Chill for at least 30 minutes
Place 3 lettuce leaves on a large plate and three on another, place half of the mixture on each set of leaves, and sprinkle 5 cherries on each salad.
Serve

name: Wali Wa Nazi
attribution: "Wali Wa Nazi" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wali_Wa_Nazi, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Wash the rice thoroughly until the water runs clear.
Soak the rice in water for 20 minutes, then drain.
In a cooking pot, combine the coconut milk, water, and salt.
Bring the mixture to a gentle boil over medium heat.
Add the drained rice and stir once.
Reduce the heat to low and cover the pot tightly.
Cook for 20–25 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Remove the pot from the heat and allow it to rest for 5–10 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork before serving.

name: Wasawasa (Yam Couscous)
attribution: "Wasawasa (Yam Couscous)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wasawasa_(Yam_Couscous), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Groundnut oil or shea butter oil

steps: Start heating a saucepan of water over medium heat so that it will begin to boil by the time the yam mixture is ready.
Sieve the yam flour into a bowl to remove any undesired particles that might be present from the processing.

Very gradually stir in water, stirring in a circular motion to form tiny grains resembling couscous. Avoid using too much water; but, if you do, you can correct with more flour. Be patient; it can take up to 10 minutes to complete. You can shake the bowl to hasten the process, so be patient and keep working until you achieve the desired texture .
Transfer the mixture to the top of a steamer over the boiling water, and then cover it for 15 minutes, lifting the lid gently after the first 10 minutes.

Take the steamer off the heat after 15 minutes, and rinse the contents in cold water to remove any remaining undesirable particles and any bitterness that the yam may occasionally have. Any clumps that may have developed are also broken up by the water. It might require two washes.
After letting it drain for a few minutes, toss with 3 teaspoons of oil and your preferred amount of salt.
Place the mixture in the steamer back over the boiling water. Cover with a fresh kitchen towel or piece of parchment paper to trap the steam, then cover with the lid. Cook for another 10–12 minutes.
Serve with any desired garnishes, such as pasta.

name: Wassel
attribution: "Wassel" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wassel, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Mix together liquid ingredients, then stir in mulling spices and orange slices.
Warm, but do not boil.
Serve hot.

name: Watalappam (Sri Lankan Coconut Custard)
attribution: "Watalappam (Sri Lankan Coconut Custard)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Watalappam_(Sri_Lankan_Coconut_Custard), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Beat the eggs in a mixer. Add the milk, brown sugar, cardamom, and cloves to the beaten eggs. Mix well.
Transfer the mixture to a pot and steam for 20 minutes. Add the cashews.

name: Watermelon Mojito Smoothie
attribution: "Watermelon Mojito Smoothie" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Watermelon_Mojito_Smoothie, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 3–4 oz water (depending how on thick you want it)

steps: Blend all ingredients together in a blender. Adjust the amount of liquid as desired.
Garnish with mint if you like.

name: Welsh Cakes
attribution: "Welsh Cakes" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Welsh_Cakes, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 450 g (2 cups or 1 lb) plain flour
170 g (¾ cup or 6 oz) castor sugar
85 g (3 oz) currants, sultanas, raisins or other dried fruit

steps: In a large mixing bowl, sift the flour then rub together with the butter and salt until mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Mix in sugar and dried fruit.
Add eggs one at a time, beating together until mixture forms a thick dough. If dough will not form, add a small amount of milk (i.e. a tablespoon).
Knead for two to three minutes until dough becomes cohesive and slightly elastic.
Roll dough out on a flat surface.
Cut 2–3-inch circles from the dough and fry
Preheat a griddle on high than lower it to medium-low (this is important to stop burning)
Griddle 2-4 minutes on each side until golden brown.

name: Welsh Fruit Bread (Bara Brith) I
attribution: "Welsh Fruit Bread (Bara Brith) I" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Welsh_Fruit_Bread_(Bara_Brith)_I, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 oz (50 g) brown sugar, plus 1 teaspoon
2 lb (900 g) loaf tin, well greased

steps: Warm the milk in a small pan until hand-hot. Put it into a bowl with 1 teaspoon of sugar and the yeast. Leave it in a warm place for about 15 minutes until a froth appears.

Sift the flour and place in a large bowl with 2 oz (50 g) sugar and the salt. Rub the fat into the flour until it resembles fine breadcrumbs, then stir in the mixed spice. Add the egg and frothed yeast. Mix to a dough in the bowl before turning it out onto a floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic. Place back into a bowl and cover with plastic film or a damp cloth. Leave it to rise in a warm place for about 90 minutes.
After it has been left to stand, 'knock down' the dough and knead again, adding the fruit slowly.
Place into a bread tin and put the tin into an oiled plastic bag. Leave to rise for about 35–40 minutes and preheat the oven to gas mark 5, 190°C (375°F).
When the dough has risen and springs back when pressed, take the tin out of the bag and bake in the centre of the oven for about 30 minutes.
Cover the top of the loaf tin with aluminium foil to stop it burning and bake for another 30 minutes.
Take out of the oven and tap the bottom of the loaf, which should sound hollow—if not, bake it for another 5 minutes.
Brush the honey onto the top of the loaf and cool it on a wire rack. Slice it thinly and serve buttered.

name: Welsh Fruit Bread (Bara Brith) II
attribution: "Welsh Fruit Bread (Bara Brith) II" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Welsh_Fruit_Bread_(Bara_Brith)_II, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 lb dried assorted fruit (e.g. raisins, cherries, etc.)

steps: Soak the fruit in the tea for 24 hours
Mix flour, sugar, egg, spice, fruit, and jam in bowl to make a batter.
Spoon batter into a loaf tin and bake for 45 minutes at 325°F.
Let cool, remove from tin, and glaze with honey.

name: Welsh Rarebit
attribution: "Welsh Rarebit" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Welsh_Rarebit, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 fl oz (60 ml) beer such as porter (Guinness will do)

steps: In a medium saucepan over low heat, melt the butter and whisk in the flour.
Cook, whisking constantly for 2–3 minutes, being careful not to brown the flour.
Whisk in mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Add beer and whisk to combine.
Pour in cream and whisk until well combined and smooth.
Gradually add cheese, stirring constantly, until cheese melts and sauce is smooth; this will take 4–5 minutes.
Pour over toast and serve immediately.

name: Wheat Modak (Coconut Pastries)
attribution: "Wheat Modak (Coconut Pastries)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wheat_Modak_(Coconut_Pastries), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine all the dough ingredients; it should be dry but should a little sticky.
Grease the dough with oil and leave covered for 1 hour.
Melt the jaggery with 4 tablespoons of water in a non-stick skillet until it is liquid.
Add coconut. Sauté for 15–20 minutes, until the mixture becomes very thick and almost dry.
Mix in the cardamom powder and remove from the fire.
Spread the mixture out on a metal tray to cool.
Take a tablespoon-sized ball of dough and roll it out—using flour if it is sticky—into a disc 4 inches across.

Put a tablespoon-sized lump of filling in the middle (it should be hardening well by now), wet the edges with a finger, and fold up the sides, crimping the dough into a peak at the top to completely seal in the filling.
Deep fry the modak in oil until golden brown.

name: Wheat-Free Baking Mix
attribution: "Wheat-Free Baking Mix" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wheat-Free_Baking_Mix, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 parts (28.5%) by weight white rice flour
2 parts (28.5%) by weight brown rice flour

steps: Combine all ingredients. Mix until very thoroughly blended.
Use the blend as a substitute for wheat flour, using the same weight of the blend as of the wheat flour; for example, if a recipe calls for 100 g wheat flour, use 100 g of this blend.

name: Whiskey Barbecue Sauce
attribution: "Whiskey Barbecue Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Whiskey_Barbecue_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine all ingredients in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat and cook, stirring, for 10 minutes.
Refrigerate in a nonreactive container for up to 2 months.

name: White Bean and Pumpkin Leaf Soup
attribution: "White Bean and Pumpkin Leaf Soup" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:White_Bean_and_Pumpkin_Leaf_Soup, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cup (or 1 handful) crayfish, finely-chopped or ground

steps: Pick over the beans to remove any debris. Transfer to a large pot, and add enough water to cover by at least 2 inches (2.5 cm).
Soak for several hours. Drain, then add fresh water.
Pound the beans for some time until you're sure it's all in little pieces.
Bring beans to a boil. Reduce heat, then simmer until beans start to soften (around ½ hour).
Add pumpkin leaves, bell peppers, any soup seasoning of your choice, chili powder, garlic, stock cubes, onions, and red oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer for ½–1 hour, until beans are soft and it's thick to your satisfaction.
Stir in cooked meat.
Serve and enjoy!

name: White Bean Soup (Bob Chorba)
attribution: "White Bean Soup (Bob Chorba)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:White_Bean_Soup_(Bob_Chorba), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: Optional: parsley, mint, sunflower oil, salt

steps: Soak the beans in cold water for 3–4 hours. Drain and cover with fresh water.
Boil beans in an earthenware pot together with the oil, finely chopped carrots, onion, and celery. Cook until beans are tender.
Add sliced peppers, grated tomatoes, and mint.
Season with salt and boil for another 15–20 minutes.
Serve sprinkled with finely-chopped parsley.

name: White Bean Soup with Basil, Rosemary, and Garlic Croutons
attribution: "White Bean Soup with Basil, Rosemary, and Garlic Croutons" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:White_Bean_Soup_with_Basil,_Rosemary,_and_Garlic_Croutons, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 cans (2 lbs) white beans, such as cannellini, drained
1 cup of your favorite marinara pasta sauce
¼ cup packed fresh basil leaves, or 1 teaspoon dried basil leaves

steps: Purée ingredients in a blender until smooth.
Pour into a large saucepan or Dutch Oven, and bring to a simmer.
Simmer, partially covered and stirring frequently, to blend flavors, 4–5 minutes.
Serve, garnished with croutons.

name: White Fish Ceviche (Cebiche de Pescado)
attribution: "White Fish Ceviche (Cebiche de Pescado)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:White_Fish_Ceviche_(Cebiche_de_Pescado), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 4 pounds (1.8 kg) of white fish (mahi mahi is an excellent choice), although most fish will work
juice from about 8 large sour green limes
3 finely-diced rocoto peppers or habanero peppers
16–24 corn cobs cut into 2-inch (5 cm) pieces, cooked as usual

steps: Wash and debone the fish, and cut it into ½ x ½ inch (about 1 x 1 cm) chunks.

Season the fish with salt, pepper, ají limo, and rocoto. Marinate the fish for a few minutes to ”cold cook” them; leaving it for too long will "overcook" the fish. You should have enough lime juice to completely cover the fish.
Add the onion and mix gently.
Serve on a bed of lettuce, and add two pieces of corn on the cob and a portion of sweet potato.

name: White Sauce
attribution: "White Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:White_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Make a white roux: melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat until the foam subsides. Add the flour and whisk together, still over the heat, for 2–3 minutes. The flour should lose its raw smell but should not brown.
Add the milk to the roux while whisking quickly but smoothly to create a smooth mixture.
Add the seasonings and cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently. Simmer the sauce until it lightly coats the back of a spoon.
Remove the bay leaf, taste and adjust for salt and pepper, and serve.

name: Whole Wheat Irish Soda Bread
attribution: "Whole Wheat Irish Soda Bread" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Whole_Wheat_Irish_Soda_Bread, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C / gasmark 3).
Use cooking spray or grease and then lightly flour a 9x5x3-inch baking pan.
Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Form a cavity in the middle.
Pour in the buttermilk.
Mix until just moistened. Too much mixing will make it tough.
Gently shape the dough to fit pan.
Cut the top at least three times with a knife.
Bake for 65–70 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the bread comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack.
Wrap in tea-towel or foil several hours or overnight for best flavor.

name: Whole Wheat Pancakes (Vegan)
attribution: "Whole Wheat Pancakes (Vegan)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Whole_Wheat_Pancakes_(Vegan), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Mix together flour, baking powder, and sugar.
Mix soy milk into the dry mixture.
Heat a griddle until water sprinkled on it quickly evaporates. Spread a thin film of oil on the griddle.
Pour pancake batter on griddle to form 2–3-inch circles. Bubbles should start forming.
When the underside is light brown, flip the pancake.
When the other side is light brown, serve.

name: Whole Wheat Waffles
attribution: "Whole Wheat Waffles" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Whole_Wheat_Waffles, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Heat waffle iron according to the manufacturer's directions.
Combine dry ingredients and mix well.
Add milk, vegetable oil, and eggs, and mix until smooth.
Pour 1 cup of batter onto the oiled waffle iron, and cook according to the manufacturer's directions.

name: Wild Spinach and Lemon Salad
attribution: "Wild Spinach and Lemon Salad" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wild_Spinach_and_Lemon_Salad, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Clean the spinach leaves and remove stems.
Blanch leaves in boiling water for 2–3 minutes.
Rinse in cold water.
Wash lemon thoroughly.
Slice lemon paper-thin with sharp knife.
Arrange plate circularly: loosely place a small bunch of leaves, then a slice of lemon, and so on.
Sprinkle with coarse ground black pepper, salt, and sumak.

name: Wilted Greens
attribution: "Wilted Greens" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wilted_Greens, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 head (3–4 cups of leaves) tat soi or any other dark leafy green, base removed (tear into smaller pieces if using a large leaf plant like chard)

steps: Rinse greens thoroughly.
Melt butter and olive oil in a wok or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and sauté until golden.
Stir in tat soi and cook, stirring constantly, until lightly wilted.
Remove from heat and cover, allowing the greens to steam in the pan for a minute or two.
When ready to serve, toss with about 1 tbsp soy sauce.

name: Windsor Pudding
attribution: "Windsor Pudding" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Windsor_Pudding, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Combine the suit, french roll, nutmeg, and lemon zest.
Mix in half a pound of apples, currants, raisins, stoned and chopped, wine, eggs, and a pinch of salt.
Mix all thoroughly together, and boil it in a basin or mould for 3 hours.
Sift fine sugar over it when sent to table, and pour a white wine sauce into the dish.

name: Wine-Roasted Pork Roast
attribution: "Wine-Roasted Pork Roast" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wine-Roasted_Pork_Roast, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Heat olive oil in 10-inch Dutch oven over campfire.
Rub seasoning on roast.
Add roast to Dutch oven, turning to brown on all sides.
Add onion, sauté 5 minutes.
Pour wine over roast.
Cover and cook slowly for three hours over fire.

name: Wisconsin Ackawi Cheese Triangles
attribution: "Wisconsin Ackawi Cheese Triangles" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wisconsin_Ackawi_Cheese_Triangles, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 cups (8 ounces / 225 g) shredded Wisconsin Ackawi cheese
½ cup (120 ml) chopped fresh parsley
¼ teaspoon (1.25 ml) ground red pepper

steps: Combine cheese, parsley, onion, egg white, and red pepper; set aside.
On a lightly floured surface, roll 1 sheet pastry into a 12 x 12-inch (30 x 30 cm) square; cut into 16 ea. 3 x 3-inch (7.5 x 7.5 cm) squares.
Place 1 tablespoon (15 ml) cheese mixture on each square; fold pastry over each filling, forming a triangle. Seal edges with tines of a fork; place on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 10 minutes or until golden brown. Repeat process with second sheet of puff pastry.
Serve warm.

name: Wow-Wow Sauce
attribution: "Wow-Wow Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Wow-Wow_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 tbsp mushroom ketchup and/or port wine

steps: Put a piece of butter as big as an egg into a saucepan. When it is melted, stir in the flour and beef broth.
Add vinegar, mushroom ketchup, and mustard. Simmer together until it is as thick as you wish.
Add the parsley and pickles, and warm them through.

name: Yam and Egg Sauce
attribution: "Yam and Egg Sauce" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yam_and_Egg_Sauce, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Peel and slice the yam. Boil yam in water until soft, then drain.
Blend the tomatoes and peppers together. Whisk together with the egg and a pinch of salt.
Cook the egg mixture in a hot pan with a little oil.
Serve the eggs with the yam.

name: Yam Casserole
attribution: "Yam Casserole" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yam_Casserole, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 2 cans (2 lb + 8 oz / 900 g) yams or sweet potatoes, drained (or 4 lb / 1.8 kg cooked, peeled, and sliced yams)

steps: In mixing bowl with electric mixer, beat yams. Add in remaining main ingredients, beating until mixture is light and fluffy. Butter a 12-inch porcelain quiche dish or a shallow 2 quart casserole dish (7x11 inches / 18 x 28 cm). Pour in yam mixture, smoothing top evenly.
Make praline topping by mixing all ingredients together in small bowl. Spread evenly over the yams. May be refrigerated covered overnight.
Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 45–50 minutes or until golden brown and bubbly.
Remove from oven and let stand 10 minutes before serving.

name: Yeasted Cornbread
attribution: "Yeasted Cornbread" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yeasted_Cornbread, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Mix water, yeast, and sugar. Let this sit for a few minutes until it bubbles.
Stir in the rest of the ingredients, adding water until it is pourable.
Bake in a greased 9×9-inch pan at 350°F (175°C, gas mark 4) for 25 minutes or until the edges turn golden brown.

name: Yeasted Kifli
attribution: "Yeasted Kifli" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yeasted_Kifli, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Mix together milk, yeast, and 1 tsp sugar, then set aside. Ensure it does not clump.
Using a pastry knife, mix flour, butter, salt in a bowl until crumbly.
Add 3½ tbsp sugar and baking powder to the flour mixture.
In a separate bowl, whisk the egg yolks. Add the yeast mixture, then the sour cream and vanilla.
Mix the wet ingredients with the dry ingredients. You should get a dough with the consistency of peanut butter cookie dough. Add additional flour if the dough is too sticky.

Knead dough well and let stand 2 hours in a warm place. To allow the dough to rise, place the bowl with the dough (covered with a tea towel) onto the top rack of the oven and place a bowl of hot water on the lower rack. Leave the oven off, and this setup will gently warm and allow the dough to rise.
Divide the dough into 5 equally-sized balls.
Sprinkle sugar on a board, put a dough ball on the board, and roll out into a circle about 12 inches across.
Flip the dough over and put more sugar on the board. Cut like a pizza into wedges about 1½ inches at the widest. Put about 1 tsp filling on each wedge and roll in sugar.
Bake on a cookie sheet at 325°F for 15 minutes or until golden brown.

name: Yeasted Rolls I
attribution: "Yeasted Rolls I" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yeasted_Rolls_I, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
steps: Knead all the ingredients together, and let rise for 1 ½ hours. Alternatively, use the dough setting on a bread machine.
Preheat oven to 350°F (177°C).
Divide dough into 12 rolls.
Brush melted butter over the top.
Bake for 20 minutes.

name: Yellow Curry Paste
attribution: "Yellow Curry Paste" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yellow_Curry_Paste, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 6 red chilli peppers, seeded and chopped

steps: Toast the cumin and coriander seeds in a pan for 3–4 minutes. Set aside.
Grind lemongrass and ginger in a mortar, add chilli-peppers and salt, and grind for 4 minutes.
Add garlic and shallot and keep grinding.
Add the roasted cumin and coriander seeds and turmeric.
Add the trassi and grind to a fluid paste.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for storage (lasts 1 month).

name: Yellow Saffron Food Coloring
attribution: "Yellow Saffron Food Coloring" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yellow_Saffron_Food_Coloring, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: ½ cup (100 g) plus 1 tablespoon white granulated sugar

steps: Use a pestle and mortar to crush the saffron and 1 tablespoon sugar together into a fine powder.
Combine the powder in a saucepan with the water and the rest of the sugar.
Turn the heat to medium-high, and stir to dissolve the sugar.
Simmer until the liquid reduces to a single-thread consistency.
Turn off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.
Cool slightly, then pour into an airtight jar and cool completely.

name: Yellow Split Pea Soup
attribution: "Yellow Split Pea Soup" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yellow_Split_Pea_Soup, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 pound (½ kilogram) dry yellow split peas

steps: Soak split peas up to six hours in cold water if you wish. This is not necessary, but will shorten cooking time.
Put all ingredients into a 6 or 8 quart stock pot or Dutch oven
Bring to a boil, then simmer covered until peas are tender, 1–2 hours.

name: Yemenite Charoset I
attribution: "Yemenite Charoset I" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yemenite_Charoset_I, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 20 g dried marjoram or oregano, partially crushed

steps: Place date spread in bowl and add crushed walnuts.
Peel the pomegranate and pound its kernels in mortar and pestle. Add to date spread.
Mix the ground cinnamon and the ground black pepper into date spread.
Add wine vinegar and dried herbs.

name: Yerushalmi Kugel (Sweet Noodle Casserole)
attribution: "Yerushalmi Kugel (Sweet Noodle Casserole)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yerushalmi_Kugel_(Sweet_Noodle_Casserole), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 8 oz (200 g) noodles (egg noodles are preferred, but others work fine as well)
⅔ cup (160 g) sugar (white sugar is helpful because it's more obvious when it begins to brown)

steps: Boil noodles according to the package instructions and drain.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan, and add ⅓ cup (80 g) sugar.
Stir continuously until the sugar begins to brown. Remove from heat.
The sugar will continue to brown for a few more minutes, creating a thick caramel.
Add the caramel to the noodles.
Add the sugar, eggs, cinnamon, pepper, and raisins. Stir.
Bake in a pan at 350°F (180°C) until the top begins to brown (about 40 minutes).

name: Yetsom Shiro (Ethiopian Vegan Chickpea Stew)
attribution: "Yetsom Shiro (Ethiopian Vegan Chickpea Stew)" from the Wikibooks Cookbook, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Yetsom_Shiro_(Ethiopian_Vegan_Chickpea_Stew), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

ingredients.display: 1 cup chickpea flour (also known as besan or gram flour)
¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
Fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped, for garnish

steps: In a dry medium-sized saucepan, toast the chickpea flour over medium heat for a few minutes until it becomes fragrant and lightly browned. Remove from heat and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in the same saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic, and sauté until the onion becomes translucent.
Stir in the berbere spice blend, paprika, turmeric, cumin, cayenne pepper, and salt. Mix well to coat the onions and garlic with the spices.
Add the toasted chickpea flour to the saucepan and stir to combine it with the spice mixture.
Gradually add the vegetable broth or water to the saucepan, stirring continuously to prevent lumps from forming.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the stew for about 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chickpea flour is fully cooked and the stew has thickened to your desired consistency.
Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt or additional spices if desired.
Remove from heat and let the stew rest for a few minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
